12. A word ending with a sixth case-affix is not compounded with a word ending with the affix 'kta,' when the force of 'kta' is to denote 'respect' &c.

The affix क् is added in the sense of inclination, understanding or respect by sūtra III. 2. 188. The present sūtra alludes to that aphorism when it uses the word पूजा: and pūjā itself is used only as an illustration and includes the other two significations of 'kta' also, namely mati 'inclination,' and buddhi 'understanding.'

As राजा मत:—बुद्ध:—पूजित: 'the king wishes, understands or respects.'

Why do we say 'when meaning respect'? When 'kta' has not this signification there is compounding. As छानहसितं 'pupil's laughing.'

वृत्ति: ॥ अधिकरणवाचिना केन षष्ठी न समस्यते ॥

13. A word ending with a sixth case-affix is not compounded with a word ending with the affix 'kta,' when the force of the latter is to denote 'locality' in which something has happened.

When the affix क् is attached to roots denoting 'fixedness, motion or eating', it gives the sense of agent and of location in connection with the action denoted by the roots i. e., that the action is located by the agent in this or that site (III. 4. 76); as इदमेषां यातम् 'here they have gone.' इदमेषां मुक्तम् 'here they have eaten.'

[ Bk. II. Ch. II. § 15, 16.

The anuvṛtti of क् does not extend to this aphorism. The word karma qualifies shashthi. Sūtra II. 3. 66 declares the conditions when, instead of the accusative, the genitive may be employed i. e., when the agent and the object of the action denoted by the nouns formed by krit affixes, are both used in a sentence, the object is put in the genitive case and not the agent; as आश्चर्य गर्वा दोहोऽगोपालकेन 'the milking of cows without a cowherd is a wonder.' रोचते ओद-नस्य भोजनं देवदत्तेन 'eating of rice agrees with Devadatta.' साधु खलु पयसः पानं देवदत्तेन 'the drinking of milk by Devadatta is indeed excellent.' विचित्रा सूत्रस्थ कृतिः पाणिनिना 'wonderful is the structure of sūtras by Pāṇini.'

तृजकाभ्यां कर्तरि ॥ १५ ॥ पदानि ॥ तृज-अकाभ्याम्, कर्तरि, (स०षष्ठी न ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्तरि या षष्ठी सा हचाऽकेन च सह न समस्यते ॥

15. A word ending with a sixth case-affix is not compounded with a word ending with 'trich' or 'aka,' when the force of the genitive case is that of an agent.

The word 'kartari' qualifies the genitive-case. The affix हच् is taught in sūtra III. 1. 133, and the affix अक is not a single affix; all affixes that have an element बु are अक; such as ण्बुवुल् or वुम् or वुन् (sūtra VII. 1. 1.) Thus भवतः शायिका 'your honor's repose' भवत आशिका 'your eating' भवतोऽमगामिका 'your going in front.'

The affix हच् is employed always in forming nouns of agency; hence there can be no example of a word in a genitive case having the force of an agent, governing another word also having the force of an agent. The हच् therefore serves no purpose in this aphorism, but applies to the sūtras that follow.

The genitive has the force of an agent under conditions mentioned in II. 3. 65.

Why do we say 'when it denotes agent'? Observe इक्षुभक्तिकां मे धारयसि.

कर्तरि च ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्तरि, च (स०षष्ठी न तृजकाभ्याम्) ॥
वृत्तिः ॥ कर्तरि च यो हजको ताभ्यां सह षष्ठी न समस्यते ॥

16. A word ending with the sixth case-affix is not compounded with a word ending with 'trich' or 'aka' affix when the force of these latter affixes is that of an agent.

The word 'kartari' qualifies the word 'aka' only and not 'trich,' for the latter always denotes the agent and nothing else.

This is a Nitya-samāsa incapable of analysis. This anuvṛtti of the word 'na' which began with sūtra 10, does not extend further. The affix हच् never has the sense of sporting or livelihood; the only examples possible are of 'aka.' 18. The indeclinable word ku 'bad,' the particles called gati, and the prepositions pra, &c., are invariably compounded with other words with which they are in construction; and the resulting compound is Tat-purusha.

The word ku means 'badness or sin'; as, कुपुरुषः 'a sinful man'; (2) Gati (I. 4. 60) as, वररकृते 'having asserted'; (I. 4. 61.) यदुरकृते ॥

So also with the words प्र &c., when they are mere particles and not used as 'upasargas,' or 'gati'; as दूर meaning 'bad,' in दुष्पुरुषः 'a bad man'; so also सु and अति meaning 'respect' in सुपुरुषः 'honorable man'; अतिपुरुषः 'excellent man'; आ means 'a little' as आपिङ्गलः 'brownish'.

Generally these are attributive words but they are found elsewhere also, as कोष्णं or कडुणम् or कद्रोष्णम् 'tepid.' So also दुष्कृतम्, अतिस्तुतम् and आवद्धम् ॥

Vart:—The words प्र &c., when the sense is that of 'gone' or the like, combine with what ends with the first case-affix. Thus प्राचार्यः 'a hereditary teacher'; so also प्रान्तेवासी.

Vart:—The words अति &c., when the thing denoted has the sense of 'gone beyond' or the like, combine with what ends with the second case affix. As अतिक्रान्तः खद्गाम् = अतिखद्गः (I. 2. 44 and 48) 'without a bed-stead,' अतिमालः 'exceeding the necklace in beauty.'

Vart:—The words अव &c., when the thing denoted is 'cried out' &c., are compounded with what ends with third case-affix as अवकुटः कोकिलया = अव कोकिलः 'what is announced by the cuckoo' i. e., the Spring.

Vart:—The words परि &c., when the thing denoted is 'weary' &c., are compounded with what ends with the fourth case-affix as परिज्ञानोऽध्ययनाय = पर्यध्ययनः 'weary of study.' अलंकुमारिः 'wealth' (sufficient to support a maiden).

Vart:—The words निर् &c., when the thing denoted is 'gone beyond' &c., are compounded with what ends with the fifth case-affix, as निष्क्रियाश्चिः 'who has gone beyond Kausāmbi'; so also निर्वाणसिः.

Vart:—A word enters into composition with इव 'like'; and there is no elision of the case-affix, and the first member of the compound retains its natural accent, as वागर्थाविव 'like a word and its meaning,' वाससीइव 'like two garments.'

Vart:—Prohibition must be stated of प्र &c., when they are 'Karma pravachaniya'; as वृक्षं प्रति विध्यन्तं विद्युत् 'the lightening flashes in the direction of the tree.' साधु देववत्तो मातरं प्रति 'Devadatta is good towards his mother.'

27. 33

BK. II. CH. II. § 19, 20.]

NITYA TAT-PURUSHA.

265.

उपपदमतिङ् ॥ १९ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपपदम्, अतिङ् ( स०त०-
निःसमर्थःसह ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपपदमतिङ्न्तं समर्पणं शब्दान्तरेण सह समस्त्यन्ते तत्पुरुषश्च समासी भवति ॥

19. An upapada or attendant word (III. 1. 92), which does not end with a tense-affix (III. 4. 78) is invariably compounded with that with which it is in construction. The compound thus formed is Tat-purusha.

Thus कुम्भकारः 'one who makes pots,' नगरकारः 'one who makes cities.'

Why do we say 'which does not end with a tense-affix'? Observe प्रधानाक्षारको ब्रजति 'he goes to bring fuel.

It might be objected, that the question of compounding with a word ending in a tense-affix is irrelevant; since the anuvritti of the words सुप् सुपा is understood here, so that तिङ् will find no scope. To this we reply that we should infer that the words सुप् सुपा should not be read into this and the last aphorism. The following Paribhāsa also arises from this sūtra.

गतिकारको पपदानां कृतिः सह समासबन्धनं प्राक् सुवृत्तपत्तेः ॥

'It should be stated that Gatis, Kārakas, and Upapadas, are compounded with bases that end with krit-affixes, before a case-termination or feminine-affix has been added to the latter.'

The result is that Upapadas and Gatis are not compounded by sūtras 18 and 19 with case-inflected nouns, but they are compounded with primary nouns before a case-termination or feminine affix is added to the latter. The same considerations apply to kārakas also. Thus अश्वक्रीती 'a female brought in exchange for a horse,' is formed correctly. अश्वेन क्रीयते सा = अश्व क्रीत; add क्रीय (IV. 1. 50) and we have अश्वक्रीती. If on the other hand, the feminine affix टॉप had been added to क्रीत previous to its composition with अश्व the form would have been अश्वक्रीता, and we should have had no base ending with short अ and in that case क्रीत could not have been added by IV. 1. 50.

अमैवाऽपयेन ॥ २० ॥ पदानि ॥ अमा, एव, अच्ययेन ( स०त०-
निरस०उपपदम् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अच्ययेनोपपदस्य यः समासः सोऽमैव भवति नान्येन ॥

20. When an upapada is compounded with an indeclinable, then it is compounded only with those avyayas which end in the affix अम्.

266

OPTIONAL TAT-PURUSHA.

[ Bk. II. Ch. II. § 20, 21.

This makes a restriction to the general compounding of upapadas with avyayas as ordained by the last rule. As स्वादुकारं मुहूक्ते 'he eats having made his food sweet.' So also लवणकारं 'having seasoned.' The avyayas ending in अम् are formed by the affix णमुल् (III. 4. 26) &c.

Why do we say 'with avyayas ending in अम्'? Observe कालो भोक्तुम् 'the time of eating.' Here the avyaya ends in उम् of the affix तुमुन् added by rule III. 3. 167 (the affix tumun may be applied, when the word in construction is not a verb, but काल, समय or वेला 'time.')

The force of the word only is to indicate that this composition takes place in those cases where a rule ordains अम् only, after any root with regard to any upapada; so that no composition will take place where the affix अम् as well as another affix is ordained after a root with certain upapadas. Thus sūtra III. 4. 24, declares: 'the affixes कृा and णमुल् come after a verb when the words अमे, प्रथम and पूर्व are upapadas.' Here the अम् (affix णमुल्) is not the sole affix ordained; but there is a co-ordinate affix with it namely कृा. Therefore in अमेभोजम् 'having first eaten' there is no composition because अमेभोजम् is not the only form we can have; for, अमेभुक्शा is also used in the same sense.

तृतीयाप्रभृतीन्यत्यतरस्याम् ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ तृतीया-प्रभृतीनि अन्यतरस्याम् ( स०त०उ०अमैवाऽप्ययेन ) ॥

पृत्तिः ॥ उपवंशस्तृतीयायामिथ्यतः प्रभृति यान्युपपदानि तान्यमैवाऽप्ययेन सहान्यतरस्यां समस्यन्ते तत्पुरुषश्च समासो भवति ॥

21. An upapada ending with a third case-affix (III. 4. 47) &c., is compounded optionally with an indefinable formed by the affix अम् and the compound is Tat-purusha.

The term अम् is understood here. The upapadas ending with a third case-affix &c., are given in sūtra III. 4. 47 and the sūtras that follow. As मूलकोपवंशं मुहूक्ते or मूलकोनोपवंशं मुहूक्ते 'he eats after having relished the food with radish.' So also पाद्वीपपीवं or पाद्वीयोरपपीवम् शेते (III. 4. 49) 'he lies pressing on his ribs.' For upapadas ending with other cases, see sūtra III. 4. 52 &c. This being an optional rule, it is not necessary that the upapada should be tulya-vidhāna with the अम्; so that this optional compounding may take place even under rule III. 4. 59 where अम् is not the only affix enjoined, but there is कृा as well. This vibhāshā may therefore be called both प्रात and अप्रात vibhāshā. It is प्रात with regard to those rules where अम् is the only affix employed; and it is अप्रात with regard to those where अम् is not the only affix.

BK II. Ch. II. § 22-24.]

BAHUBRIHI.

कृ. च ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ कृ. च, ( स०त०तृतीयाप्रभृतीन्य-
न्यतरस्यान् उप० ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कृ.प्रत्ययेन सह दत्तोवा प्रभृतीन्युपदानि अन्यतरस्यां समस्यन्ते तत्पुरुषश्च
समासो भवति ॥

22. An upapada ending with a third case-affix
or any other of the remaining four cases, is optionally
compounded with a word ending with the affix ktvā;
and the compound is Tat-purusha.

This rule provides for avyayas ending in कृ. which the last two rules
did not provide. Thus we have उच्चैः कुरु or उच्चैः कुरुा. Here the affix कृ. is
added by sūtra III. 4. 59. In the case when there is composition, the कृ. is
replaced by the substitute ल्यप्; otherwise not. See VII. 1. 37.

The condition of the upapadas being in the 3rd case &c., applies
here also. Therefore there is no composition in अल् कुरुा or खलु कुरुा.

शेषो बहुव्रीहिः ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ शेषः, बहुव्रीहिः ( स० ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ शेषः समासो बहुव्रीहिसंज्ञी भवति ॥

23. The remaining compound is called Bahu-
vrihi.

A compound which does not fall within any one of the rules given
above, will be Bahuvrihi. This is a governing aphorism and extends up to
sūtra 28. Thus चित्रणः 'possessed of a brindled cow.'

अनेकमन्यपदार्थे ॥ २४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अनेकम्, अन्य-पद-अर्थे ( स०-

वार्तिकम् ॥ बहुव्रीहिः समानाधिकरणानामिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अन्ययानां च बहुव्रीहिरवक्तव्यः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ समन्युपमानपूर्वपदस्थोवरपदश्लोपश्च वक्तव्यः ॥

24. Two or more words, ending in any case-
affix, form a compound, denoting another new thing,
not connoted by those words individually; and the com-
pound is called Bahuvrihi.

263

BAHUVRIHI.

[ Bk. Ch. I. § 24.

The Bahuvrīhi compound comes with the force of all the affixes but the first; as प्रातृवृकं मानं = प्रातोदको मानः 'a water-reached village.' ऊढरथोऽनङ्गन् 'a bull by whom a cart is drawn.' उधृतपशुकृदः 'Rūdra to whom cattle is offered.' ऊडुतोदना स्थाली 'a vessel in which rice is placed.' चित्रगुडवदतः 'Devadatta possessed of a brindled cow.' वीरपुरुषको मानः 'a village possessed of heroic men.'

Bahuvrīhi compound is not formed with the sense of the first case. As बृटे देवे गतः 'gone when it had rained.'

Why do we say 'more than one'? So that there may be compounding of many words, as in the following verse:—

सुसुद्वजटकेसैन सुलभाजिनवाससा । पुत्री पर्वतराजस्य कुतो हेतोर्विवाहिता ॥..

'Why was the daughter of the king of the mountains married by Siva possessed of beautifully-delicate-locked-hair, and cheap-deer-skin-dress.'

Vart:—Bahuvrīhi compounds are formed of words having the same case, so that words not being in apposition are not so compounded; as पंचनिर्मुक्तमस्य .

Vart:—The compounds of indeclinables are Bahuvrīhi; as उच्चैर्मुखः 'possessed of raised mouth.' So also नीचैर्मुखः &c.

Vart:—The second member is elided in a Bahuvrīhi compound of which the first member is a word in the locative case, or a word with which comparison is made (उपमान). As, कण्ठे स्थितः कालोऽस्य = कण्ठे कालः 'in whose throat there is blackness (Siva).' उरसिलोमः 'who has hair on his chest.' उष्ट्रस्य मुखमिव मुखं यस्य सः = उष्ट्रमुखः 'he whose face is like that of a camel.' खरमुखः 'ass-faced.'

Vart:—Bahuvrīhi compound may be formed after eliding the second member with a word in the sixth case denoting 'collection or modification.' As केशानां संधातः = केशसंघातः , केशसंघातभूवाऽस्य = केशचूद्रः 'he who has a collection of hair as crest.' सुवर्णस्य विकारोऽर्जकारोऽस्य = सुवर्णजंकारः 'he who has ornaments made of gold.'

Vart:—The optional compounding of what arises from a verbal root coming after प्र &c. should be stated, and the elision of the subsequent term. As प्रवतितं पर्यायस्य = प्रपर्णः 'a tree of which the leaves are all fallen.' So also प्रपलाशः .

Vart:—The compounding of words signifying what exists, coming after the negative नम्र should be stated, and the optional elision of the second of the terms. As, अविधमान पुत्री यस्य = अपुनः 'childless.' So also अमाव्यैः 'wife-less.'

Vart:—Compounds like अस्तिक्षीरा should be stated as Bahuvrīhi. As अस्तिक्षीरा श्रापणी 'a Brāhmaṇī having milk.' These words are indeclinables. The word 'asti' here is an indeclinable though appearing as a verb.

BK. II. CH. II. § 25, 26.]

BAHUVRIHI.

269

संख्यायव्ययासन्नादूराधिकसंख्याः संख्येये ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥

संख्यया, अव्यय-आसन्न-अदूर-अधिक-संख्याः, संख्येये, (स०बहुथ्रीहि:सह) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ संख्येये या संख्या वर्तते तथा सहाव्ययासन्नादूराधिकसंख्याः समस्यन्ते बहुथ्रीहिश्च समासो भवति ॥

25. Indeclinable words and the words *âsanna* 'near,' *adûra* 'near,' *adhika* 'more' and the words called *saṅkhyâ* (Numerals) are compounded with another *saṅkhyâ* word, when the sense is that of a numeral or *saṅkhyâ*. The compound is *Bahuvrīhi*.

Thus उपदेशाः (V. 4. 73) 'those who are near ten *i.e.* nine or eleven.' Similarly उपदेशाः 'nineteen or twenty-one' (VI. 4. 142). So also आसन्नदेशाः 'nine or eleven.' अदूरदेशाः 'nine or eleven.' अधिकदेशाः 'eleven.'

So also two 'numerals' may be compounded; as, द्विजाः 'two or three.' द्विदशाः 'twenty.'

Why do we say 'with a numeral'? Observe पंच ब्राह्मणाः 'five Brâh-manas.'

Why do we say 'with an Indeclinable &c'? Witness ब्राह्मणाः पंच. Why do we say 'when denoting a numeral'? Observe अधिका विशति गैवाम् 'of cows more than twenty.'

दिङ्नामान्यन्तराले ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ दिङ्नामानि, अन्तराले (स०बहुथ्रीहि) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दिङ्नामानि सुबन्तानि अन्तराले वाष्ये समस्यन्ते बहुथ्रीहिश्च समासो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ सर्वनाम्नो वृत्तिमात्रे पुंयद्वावः ॥

26. Words which are the names of the points of the compass are compounded, when the compound signifies the intermediate point, and the compound so formed is *Bahuvrīhi*.

Thus दक्षिणपूर्वादिक् *dakshina-pūrvā*, 'south-east,' (the direction midway between south and east.) पूर्वोत्तरा 'north-east.'

The word नाम is introduced in the *sūtra* to indicate that no compounding takes place when the words denoting direction are derivative words whose primary signification is not indicative of direction; as ऐन्द्रध्वकोबेर्याध्व विशोर्वदन्तराजम् 'the point between east and north.' Here the words ऐन्द्रि 'east' and कोबेरी 'north' though denoting directions, are derivatively so, and hence no compounding.

BAHUVRIHI.

[ Bk. II. Ch. II. § 27, 28.

*Vart*:—Whenever a Bahuvrīhi gets the designation of Sarvanāman (I. 1, 28, 29), the first term becomes masculine, by VI. 3. 34; as दक्षिणा + पूर्वा = दक्षिणपूर्वा ॥

तत्र तेनेदमिति सरूपे ॥ २७ ॥ पदानि ॥ तत्र, तेन, इदम्, इति, सरूपे ( स०बहुञ्जीहि: ) ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ तत्रेति स०स्थन्ते सरूपे परे तेनेति च द्वितीयान्ते इदमित्येतस्मिन्नये समस्थते बहुञ्जीहिश्च समासो भवति ॥

27. Two homonymous words (both being in the locative case or both being in the instrumental case) are compounded, the sense being 'this happens therein or with that.' The compound so formed is Bahuvrīhi.

The word तत्र means 'a word in the locative case,' and तेन 'a word in the instrumental case.' The word सरूप or 'similar form' applies to both. The word इति indicates that the meaning of the compound so formed should be learned from popular usage, therefore it means, 'seizing, striking, fighting.' All these senses are implied by इति. The word is exhibited in the locative case, if the sense is that of seizing; and the word is exhibited in the instrumental case, when the sense is that of striking; the word indicated by the word इदमिति is युद्ध; as केशोघुकेशोघु च गृहीत्वा इदं युद्धं वृत्तं = केशाकेशि (VI. 3. 137 and V. 4. 127.) 'hair to hair, fighting by pulling each other's hair'; कचाकचि 'hair against hair'; एण्डैथ-एण्डैथ प्रहृत्य इदं युद्धं वृत्तं = एण्डाइण्डि 'stick against stick, fight with stick and stave;' so also मृगालामृगाली. In the above examples the samāsānta affix इच् is added at the end by rule V. 4. 127; and all such words are Avyaya or indeclinable. The final vowel of the first term is lengthened by Rule VI. 3. 137.

Why do we say 'having the same form'? We cannot form such a compound from the following: इलेक्ष मुपलेक्ष प्रहृत्य इदं युद्धं वृत्तम्.

तेन सहेति तुल्ययोगे ॥ २८ ॥ पदानि ॥ तेन, सह-इति, तुल्य-योगे, ( स०बहुञ्जीहि: ) ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ सहेत्येतच्छकुरूपं तुल्ययोगे वर्तम-नं तेनेति द्वितीयान्तेन स० समस्थते बहुञ्जीहिश्च समासो भवति ॥

28. The word saha 'together' is compounded with a word ending with the third case-affix and the compound is Bahuvrīhi; provided that, the companion and the person accompanied are equally affected by any action or thing, in the same manner.

BK. II. CH. II. § 28-30.]

PURVA-NIPATA IN DVANDVA.

271

Thus सह पुत्रेणागतः = सुषः (VI. 3. 82, सह changed to स) 'he has come accompanied by his son'. सच्चानः 'accompanied by the pupil.' सकर्मकः 'accompanied by the servant.'

Why do we say 'tulya-yoga'? Witness सहैव दग्निः पुत्रैर्भारि बहति गर्वनी 'the she-ass carries the whole burden, though there exist her ten sons.'

How do we get the forms like सकर्मकः, सलोमकः, सपत्तकः &c., in which there is no 'tulya-yoga'? It shows that this condition is of limited operation (तुल्य गोगवचनं प्रायिकं).

चार्ये द्वन्द्वः ॥ २९ ॥ पदानि ॥ च-अर्थे, द्वन्द्वः, (स०अनेकम्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अनेकं सुबन्धं चार्ये वर्त्तमानं समस्थते इन्द्रश्च समासी भवति ॥

29. When a set of several words ending with case-affixes stands in a relation expressible by 'and' the set is made into a compound; and the compound so formed is called Dvandva.

The meanings that may be indicated by 'and' are four, (1) समुच्चयः 'community of reference,' (2) अन्वाचयः 'collateralness of reference,' (3) इतरेतरयोगः 'mutual conjunction' and (4) समाहारः 'aggregate.' In the first two cases viz., community of reference, and collateralness of reference, composition does not take place, because the words are not directly related to one another (II. 1. 1). Composition is enjoined therefore, when the sense of च is that of mutual conjunction and lumping. Thus we cannot compound ईश्वरं गुरुं च भजस्व 'reverence God and thy Guru' or भिज्ञामहं गां चानय 'go for alms and bring the cow.' But we can compound the following प्रश्नश्च न्यमोऽप्य = प्रश्नच्यमोऽप्य 'the Plaksha and the Nyagrodha trees.' So धव-खदिर-पलाशाः, वाक्यचम्, वाग्द्रपदम् ॥

उपसर्जनं पूर्वम् ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ उपसर्जनम्, पूर्वम् (समासः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्जनसंज्ञकं समासे पूर्वं प्रयोक्तव्यम् ॥

30. The upasarjana (I. 2. 43) is to be placed first in a compound.

The word समासे is understood here. The upasarjana being the word exhibited in the nominative case in the rules relating to samāsa, must stand first. The constant application of this rule has been illustrated in the previous aphorisms. Without this rule, there would have been no fixity as to the position of words.

राजदन्तादिषु परम् ॥ ३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ राजदन्त-आदिषु, परम्, (स०उपसर्जनम्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ राजदन्तादिषु परमुपसर्जनं प्रयोक्तव्यम् ॥

As हरिहरौ 'Hari and Hara.' So also पदुमुतौ and मुदुमुतौ. Where there are more than one such चि words in a compound, any one may be fixed upon as first member, and the rest to follow no fixed rule. As पदुमुदुमुक्काः or पदुमुक्कमुववः.

Why do we say 'Dvandva'? Observe विस्तरपदुः which is Tat-purusha.

वार्तिकम् ॥ बहुव्यनियमः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ द्वन्द्वेयजाद्यदन्तं विप्रतिषेधेन ॥

33. In a Dvandva compound, let what begins with a vowel and ends with a short अ be placed first.

BR. II. CH. II. § 33, 34.] PURVA-NIPATA IN DVANDVA.

273

Thus, उध्द्रखरम् 'the camel and the ass,' उध्द्रशाकम् 'the camel and the hare.'

Vart:—When there are may such words there is no fixed rule. As अयवरघेन्दाः or इन्द्रयारवाः.

Vart:—In the Dvandva compounds the चि would stand first only then, when the rule of अजायदन्त does not prohibit it. Thus इन्द्राग्नी or इन्द्रवायू. Here अग्नि and वायु though चि, do not stand first, because इन्द्र beginning with a vowel and ending in short अ, by the rule of vipratishedha takes precedence (I. 4. 2).

Why do we say 'अन्त् with a त्व्' (I. 1. 70)? This rule does not apply when it is long आ as अयवा + वृषः = अयवावृषी or वृषारवे.

अल्पाच्चतरम् ॥ ३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अल्पाच्चतरम्, (सङ्घन्देपूर्वम्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अल्पाच्चतरं शब्दरूपं इन्द्रे समासे पूर्वप्रयोक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ कृतुनज्ज्ञाणामानुपूर्व्येण समानान्तराणां पूर्वनिपातो वक्तव्यः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ लभ्यन्तरं पूर्वं निपततीति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अभ्यहिंतं च पूर्वं निपततीति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ वर्णानामानुपूर्व्येण पूर्वनिपातः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ धातुभ्य व्यायसः पूर्वनिपातो वक्तव्यः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ संख्याया अल्पीयस्याः पूर्वनिपातो वक्तव्यः ॥

34. In a Dvandva compound, that word-form which has fewer vowels, is to be placed first.

Thus प्रश्न+न्यधीध = प्रजन्यमोधी; and धवखदिरपलाशाः ॥

When there are many words, there is no fixed rule. As शंखवुन्दुभिवीणाः or वीणाशंखवुन्दुभयः.

Vart:—Names of seasons and stars consisting of equal number of syllables should be arranged in the compound according to their natural order of succession. As हेमन्तशिशिरवसन्ताः; चित्राख्याती; कृतिकारोहिण्यौ.

When they do not consist of equal syllables, the shorter should be placed first; as भीष्मवसन्तौ.

Vart:—A word consisting of light (laghu) vowels is placed first. As, कुशकाशं; शरशादम्.

Vart:—The more honorable of the two is placed first; as, मातापितरौ 'mother and father,' अद्वानेधे 'faith and intelligence' दीक्षातपसी 'initiation and austerity'.

Vart:—The castes are placed according to their order: as, ब्राह्मणशक्तिः विद् शुक्लः 'Brāhmaṇa Kshatriya Vaiśya and Sudra.' There is no limitation of equality of syllables here.

Vart:—The name of the elder brother is placed first; as युधिष्ठिरार्जुनैः 'Yudhishthira and Arjuna.'

Vart:—Among numerals, the less in value is placed first; as द्विजा 'two; and three'; त्रिचतुरा 'three and four.'

वृत्तिः ॥ सप्तम्यन्तं विशेषणं च बहुव्रीहिसमासे पूर्वं प्रयोज्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ सर्वनामसंख्ययोरुपसंख्यानम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ वा प्रियस्य पूर्वनिपातः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ सप्तम्या: पूर्वनिपाते प्राते गङ्गाविभ्यः सप्तम्यन्तं परम् ॥

35. A word with the seventh case-affix and an epithet are to be placed first in the Bahuvrīhi compound.

In a Bahuvrīhi, all words are upasarjana, and hence there is no rule for their arrangement. The present aphorism declares that rule; as कण्ठकालः 'who is black in the throat.' So also उरशिलोमा, चित्रगुः, शबलगुः.

Vart:—The sarvanāmas and the numerals stand first; as सर्वव्रतेः, सर्वकृष्णः, द्विगुणः, द्विकृष्णः. In a compound formed by the composition of sarvanāma words with a saṅkhya word, the latter should stand first; as, द्रव्यः, ध्वन्यः &c.

Vart:—The word प्रिय may optionally stand first; as गुडप्रियः or प्रियगुडः.

Vart:—After the words गङ्ग &c., the word in the 7th case-affix comes as subsequent; as गङ्गकण्ठः 'a hump-necked'; गङ्गशिराः &c.

How is then the word बहेगङ्गः 'hump in the shoulder' to be explained? This is governed by the general rule, and not the exceptional vārtika.

निष्ठा, ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ निष्ठा, ( स०बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वम् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ निष्ठान्तं च बहुव्रीहिसमासे पूर्वं प्रयोज्यम् ॥

ॐ

# ॥ अथ द्वितीयाध्यायस्य तृतीयः पादः ॥

# BOOK SECOND.

# CHAPTER III.

अनभिहिते ॥ १ ॥ पदानि ॥ अन-अनभिहिते ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अनभिहित इत्यभिकारोऽयं वेदितव्यः । यदित उद्वेगमनुभविनियोजोऽनभिहित इत्येवं
सद्भेदितव्यम् ॥

1. The word 'anabhihite' meaning 'not being specified' is to be understood as the governing word.

Whatever will be taught from this point forward, should be understood to apply to those cases which have not been specified otherwise. The case-affixes like those denoting 'object' 'instrument' &c., are applied to a noun, only then, when the force of the case-affix is not otherwise denoted or mentioned or exhibited. The force of a case-affix may be so denoted either by first, the conjugational affixes तिक्; secondly, by the Primary affixes or कृत, thirdly, by the secondary affixes तद्वित; or lastly by compounds. Thus sūtra 2 declares that the second case-affix is applied in denoting the object, as कटं करोति 'he makes the mat'; प्रान गच्छति 'he goes to the village.' But the object can otherwise be denoted. Thus by the passive conjugational affix, as कृते कटः 'the mat is made.' Here the termination of the verb denotes the object. See sūtra I. 3. 13. and III. 4. 69. So also by the krit affix, as कृतः कटः 'the mat is made,' see Sūtra III. 4. 70. So also by a Taddhita affix as सत्य or मतिकः meaning 'purchased with a hundred' = यतेन क्रीतः. Similarly by samāsa, as मासभुदकं प्रानम् = मासोदको प्रानः ॥

कर्मणि द्वितीया ॥ २ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्मणि, द्वितीया ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्मणि कारते वा संध्या तत्र द्वितीया विभक्ति भेदति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ उभयवर्तयाः कार्यं पितृपर्यादिषु भिषु ।

द्वितीयाऽग्रे द्वितान्तेषु ततोऽन्यत्रापि दृश्यते ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अभितः-परितः-समया-निकषा-हा-प्रति-योगेषु च दृश्यते ॥

2. When the object is not denoted by the termination of the verb, i e. when the verb does not agree with it, the second case-affix is attached to the word.

278

ACCUSATIVE CASE.

[BK. II. CH. III. § 2-4.]

The terms dvitiyā &c., are technical phraseology of older grammarians, and hence not defined by Pāṇini; they apply to the triads of युग affixes. क्तं करोति 'he makes the mat,' ग्रामं गच्छति 'he goes to the village.'

The words उभयतः, सर्वतः, भिक्षु and the double forms उपर्युपरि, अभोषः, अभ्यभि, when they have the sense of nearness, govern the accusative. Sometimes other cases also, as उभयतो ग्रामं 'on both sides of the village'; सर्वतो ग्रामं 'on all sides of the village'; भिन्देवदत्तं 'fie to Devadatta'; उपर्युपरि ग्रामं 'just over the village'; अभ्यभि or अभोषो ग्रामं 'just below the village.'

Vart:—The words अभितः, परितः both meaning 'round', समया, भिक्षा both meaning 'near', and हा 'woe be to,' and प्रति 'to,' govern the accusative case; as, अभितो ग्रामं 'round the village,' ग्रामं समया 'near the village'; हा देवदत्तं 'woe be to Devadatta'; युगभितम् न प्रतिभाति किंचित् 'to a hungry person nothing occurs to his mind.' See I. 4. 49 &c.

तृतीया च होइछन्दसि ॥ ३ ॥ पदानि ॥ तृतीया, च, होः, छन्दसि, ( कर्मणि ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छन्दसि विपये जुहोतेः कर्मणि कारके तृतीया विभक्ति भैयति द्वितीया च ॥

3. In the chhandas (veda), the object of the verb hu 'to sacrifice' takes the affix of the third case, and of the second as well.

This ordains the third case-affix, and by force of the word च 'and' the second case-affix is also employed as यथावागिनहोतं जुहोति 'he satisfies or pleases Agni with barley-powder,' or यथावागिनहोतं जुहोति 'he throws barleypowder into the fire as oblation.'

Why do we say 'in the vedas?' In the classical Sanskrit, the accusative only must be used and not the instrumental.

अन्तराऽन्तरेणयुकृते ॥ ४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अन्तरा, अन्तरेण, युकृते, ( द्विवितीया )

वृत्तिः ॥ अन्तराऽन्तरेणयुकृते निपाती साङ्ग्रयाद् युकृते । अभ्यभि योगे द्वितीया विभक्ति भैयति ॥

4. A word joined with (or governed by) the word antarā, or antareṇa takes the second case-affix.

The anuvṛtti of dvitiyā is understand here and not that of tritiyā. Both these words antarā and antareṇa are Nipātas. They govern the accusative. This debars the genitive case. The word antarā means 'between' while antareṇa means 'besides that,' 'without,' 'exception,' 'with reference to' 'regarding.' As, अन्तरेण युगकारं न किंचित्सम्बन्धे nothing can be

BK. II. CH. III. § 5-6 ]

ACCUSATIVE CASE.

279

gained without exertion. अन्तर्‍रा or अन्तर्‍रेण्‍त्‍वां च नांव कर्मवृक्षुः 'the bowl is between thee and me.' कोऽन्यस्त्वां नां तरेण्‍त्‍यं यक्तः प्रतिकर्तुं 'who else but thee is able to retaliate.'

Why do we say 'when joined with?' Observe अन्तर्‍रा तद्वशिलांष्‍ पादलिपुत्रं खुचन्तस्य प्राकारः.

कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे ॥ ५ ॥ पदानि ॥ काल-अध्वनोः, अत्यन्त-संयोगे, (द्वितीया) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ काल-शब्देभ्योऽध्वशब्देभ्यश्च द्वितीया विभक्तिर्भवति अत्यन्तसंयोगे गन्धमाने ॥

5. After a word denoting time, or length, the affix of the 2nd case is employed, when denoting full duration.

भावनपीते 'he reads for a month,' 'he studies full one month,' भावं काल्पाणी 'prosperous during the month' (uninterruptedly), संवत्सरं पुष्पाः 'flowers during the year continually,' क्रोधं कुटिला नदी 'the river winding for one kos without any break,' क्रोधं पर्वतः 'the hill through one full kos.' यथा वैष्णवणी राजन् शतयोजनमायता 'O king the hall of Viśravana is 100 yojanas in length.

The word अत्यन्तसंयोग or 'full continuity' means the complete relation of time or space with its action, attribute or substance.

Why do we say 'atyanta-sanyoga or complete continuity'? Observe भावस्य द्वितीये or क्रोधस्यैकदेशे पर्वतः ॥

अपवर्गे तृतीया ॥ ६ ॥ पदानि ॥ अपवर्गे, तृतीया, (कालाध्वनो रत्यन्तसंयोगे) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अपवर्गे गन्धमाने कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे तृतीया विभक्तिर्भवति ॥

6. The third case-affix is employed after the words denoting the duration of time or place, when the accomplishment of the desired object is meant to be expressed.

भावेनातुवाकोऽपीतः 'he learnt the Anuvāka in a month,' क्रोधेनातुवाकोऽपीतः 'he learnt the Anuvāka by going over a kos.

The word अपवर्ग means 'the finishing of an action, on the attainment of the object intended by the action, but not before.' Thus संवत्सरेणातुवाकोऽपीतः means 'Anuvāka was perseveringly and effectually read by him in the whole year.'

When the idea of apavarga is not intended, the accusative case is employed, as भावनपीतेऽतुवाकः 'learnt for a month, but not yet completed, the Anuvāka.'

280

ACCUSATIVE CASE.

[BK. II. CH. III. § 7-9.

सममीपञ्चमयी कारकमध्ये ॥ ७ ॥ पदानि ॥ सममी-पञ्चमयी, कारक-मध्ये, ( कालाध्वनोर० ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कारकयोरमध्ये यो कालाध्वनरी ताभ्यां सममी पञ्चमयी विभक्ती भवतः ॥

7. A noun denoting time or place gets the affix of the seventh or the fifth case, when the sense implied is that the time or space is the interval between one action and another action (or implies an interval of time and space between two karakas).

Ex. अदा भुक्ता देवदत्तो दा बडे दा बडाद्वायोक्ता 'having dined today, Devadatta will dine in or after two days.' Here the 'time' is the interval between the agent and his power of eating. So also इदस्योऽयनिम्बानः कोयात् कोये वा स्वयं विधयेत् 'standing here, he will hit a mark at the distance of one kos., Here kos is the interval between the agent and the object or the object and the ablation, or the object and the location. The rule 1. 3. 10 does not apply here.

कर्मप्रवचनीययुक्ते द्रुवितीया ॥ ८ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्मप्रवचनीय-युक्ते, द्रुवितीया ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्मप्रवचनीयैर्मु के द्वितीया विभक्तिर्भवति ॥

8. The second case-affix is employed after a word which is joined with a karmapravachaniya (I. 4. 83).

Ex. याकल्पस्य संहितामनुमाययेत् 'It rained on (hearing) the reading of the Veda by Sakalya.' So also आगस्त्वमन्वभि चत् प्रजा ॥

यस्मादधिकं यस्य चैश्वरवचनं तत्र सप्तमी ॥ ९ ॥ पदानि ॥ यस्माद्-अधिकं, यस्य, च, ईश्व र-वचनं, तत्र, सप्तमी, (कर्मप्रवचनीययुक्ते) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यस्मादधिकं यस्य चैश्वरवचनं कर्मप्रवचनीयैर्मु के तत्र सप्तमी विभक्तिर्भवति ॥

9. Where a word is governed by a karmapravachaniya in the sense of 'more than' (I. 4. 87) or 'lord of' (I. 4. 97) there the 7th case-affix (locative) is employed.

Ex. उपलायोत् प्रोचः 'A Dropa is more than a Khāri,' अभिन्नदत्ते पंचालाः 'Brahmadatta is the lord of Panchālas.' The phrase यस्यचैश्वर वचनं indicate that both the thing owned and the owner may be in the locative. So I. 4. 97.

This aphorism debars the accusative.

BK. II. CH. III. § 10-12.]

ABLATIVE CASE.

281

पञ्चमपाङ्गुपरिभिः ॥ १० ॥ पदानि ॥ पञ्चमी, अप-आङ्गु-
परिभिः, ( कर्मप्रवचनीययु० ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अप आङ्गु परि इत्येतैः कर्मप्रवचनीययेये पञ्चमी विभक्तिभवति ॥

10. The fifth case-affix (Ablative) is employed when a word is governed by the following karmapravachantyas *i.e.*, apa, ān and pari.

Ex. अप or आ or परि पाटलिपुत्रादाबुद्धो देवः 'It rained off or upto or with the exclusion of, Pātaliputra.

The परि here has the meaning of 'exclusion' (I. 4. 88) being read along with अप, therefore, not here इयं परि विद्योतते विद्वान् (I. 4. 90).

प्रतिनिधिप्रतिदाने च यस्मात् ॥ ११ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रति-निधि-
प्रतिदाने, च, यस्मात् ( कर्मप्र० ) ( पञ्चमी ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यस्मात्प्रतिनिधिर्यतद्व प्रतिदानं तत्र कर्मप्रवचनीययुतो पञ्चमी विभक्तिभवति ॥

11. The 5th case-affix (ablative) is employed after what soever is governed by a karmapravachantya in the sense of 'substitute' or 'exchange' (I. 4. 92).

Ex. अभिभ्युरञ्जुनतः प्रति 'Abhimanyu is the representative of Arjuna.'
भावानस्मैतिकेभ्यः प्रतिपञ्चति 'he exchanges māshās for this sesamum.' See I. 4. 92 for an explanation of प्रतिनिधि and प्रतिदान.

गत्यर्थकर्मणि द्वितीयाचतुष्ट्यौ चेष्टायामनध्वनि ॥ १२ ॥ पदानि ॥
गत्यर्थ-कर्मणि, द्वितीया-चतुष्ट्यौ, चेष्टायाम्, अनध्वनि ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गत्यर्थानां पादानां चेष्टाक्रियायां परिरूपनङ्क्रियायां कर्मणि कार्लेऽप्यवर्तिते
द्वितीयाचतुष्ट्यौ भवतः

12. In the case of roots implying motion, the place to which motion is directed takes the affix of the 2nd (Accusative) or the 4th (Dative) case in denoting the 'object,' when physical motion is meant, and the object is not a word expressing 'road'.

Ex. ग्रामं or ग्रामाय गच्छति 'he goes to the village.' But not so in जनया हरिं
बुजति (the verb not denoting physical motion) 'he goes mentally to Hari'
अध्यानं गच्छति 'he goes over the way' (the object being the 'way'). But not
so in ओहनं पचति 'he cooks rice,' (the verb not denoting 'motion') nor in
अस्येन बुजति (the verb not denoting 'the object.')

DATIVE CASE.

[BK. II. CH. III. § 20, 12-14.

Note.—The word adhvan includes the synonyms of road (I. 1. 68) as पश्चात्, गच्छति, नागे गच्छति.

Note.—The prohibition applies with regard to the going over or occupying the road; so that where a person from a wrong road goes to the right road, there the fourth case-affix will be employed as पये गच्छति.

चतुर्थी संप्रदाने ॥ १३ ॥ पदानि ॥ चतुर्थी, संप्रदाने ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ संप्रदाने कारके चतुर्थी विभक्तिर्भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ चतुर्थी विधाने तादृशं उपसंख्यानम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ क्षुपिसंपदनाने चतुर्थी वक्तव्या ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ उत्पातेन साभ्यनाने चतुर्थी वक्तव्या ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ हितयोगे चतुर्थी वक्तव्या ॥

13. In denoting the sampradāna-kāraka (I. 4. 32.) the fourth affix, or the Dative is employed after the noun.

Ex. उपाध्यायाय गां ददाति 'He gives a cow to the teacher' देवदत्ताय रोचते 'it pleases Devadatta' (I. 4. 33) पुरुषेभ्यः स्पृहयति (I. 4. 36) 'he desires flowers.

Vart.—The fourth case-affix should be employed when the sense is that of 'for the purpose thereof' as ध्रुवाय दास 'wood is for making posts.' कुण्डलाय हिरण्यं 'gold used for the purpose of making ear-ring.' रन्धनाय स्थाली 'pot for the sake of cooking.' अवहननायोलुललं 'mortar for the sake of threshing.'

Vart.—The verb क्षुप and other verbs meaning 'to be fit or adequate for, result in, bring about, accomplish, produce, tend to,' govern the dative case: as, भुजाय कल्पते यवागुः 'the barley gruel tends to produce urine.' So also भुजाय संपदाते जावते वा यवागुः.

Vart.—The fourth case-affix is employed with the force of 'indicating a portent or calamity,' as.

वाताय कपिला विद्वद् दातपायाति लोहिनी ॥

पीता वर्धाय विधेया दुर्भिक्षाय सिता मतेऽ ॥

'The reddish lightening portends wind, extremely red indicates heat, yellow portends rain and white lightening prognosticates famine.'

Vart.—The fourth case-affix should be employed in connection with the word हित: as गोप्येऽहितं 'good for cows.'

क्रियार्थोपपदस्य च कर्मणि स्थानिनः ॥ १४ ॥ पदानि ॥ क्रिया-अर्थ-उपपदस्य, च, कर्मणि, स्थानिनः, (चतुर्थी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ क्रियार्थोपपदस्य च स्थानिनोऽप्रयुग्मानस्य पातोः कर्मणि कारके चतुर्थी विभक्तिर्भवति ॥

Bk. II. Ch. III § 14-15.]

DATIVE CASE.

283

14. The fourth case-affix is employed in denoting the object (karma) of that verb, which is suppressed (sthāni) in a sentence, and which has in construction (upapada) therewith another verb, denoting an action, performed for the sake of the future action (kriyārtha III. 3. 10.).

In other words, when the sense of an infinitive of purpose formed by 'tumun' and 'nvul' (III. 3. 10.) is suppressed in a sentence, the object of this infinitive is put in the Dative case.

फ्लैभ्यो बुजति=फलान्याहुतुं बुजति 'he goes for fruits i. e., to bring fruits.' This debars the accusative case. So also we have फ्लैभ्यो बुजति 'he goes for fuel.' The words क्रियायोपदस्य and स्थानिनः are in apposition. The first is a Bahuvrīhi compound of क्रियायोपदस्य and means 'a verb whose upapada denotes the purpose of the action (kriyārtha).' Thus in फलान्याहुतुं 'to bring fuel'; the infinitive verb आहुतुं 'is क्रियायोपदस्य, the object of this verb is पयः when this verb is suppressed, it becomes स्थानिनः; the object of this verb takes the fourth case-affix.

Why do we say 'of the verb whose upapada denotes the purpose of the action? Observe प्रविधि पिंडीच्.

Why do we say 'in denoting the object.' Witness फ्लैभ्यो बुजति यकटेन 'for fuel he goes with a cart.'

Why do we 'when suppressed?' Observe फलान्याहुतुं बुजति.

तुमर्थाच्च भाववचनात् ॥ १५ ॥ पदानि ॥ तुम-अर्थात्, च भाव-घचनात्, (चतुर्थी) ॥

बुजिः ॥ तुमर्थभाववचनतत्त्वानात् प्रातिपदिकाच्चतुर्थी विभक्ति भंवति ॥

15. The fourth case-affix is employed after a crude-form which ends in an affix denoting 'condition' (abstract noun. III. 3. 11.) and having the force of the affix tum (or Infinitive of purpose).

Ex. यानाय बुजति 'he goes to offer a sacrifice' = यदु' बुजति. So also स्थानाय बुजति, भूतये बुजति.

The word तुमर्थ means 'means' having the same significance as the affix युष.

नमःस्वस्तिस्वहास्वधालंवपडयोगाच्च ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ नमः-स्वस्ति-स्वाहा-स्वधा-अलम्-वपड-योगात्, च, (चतुर्थी) ॥

चिः ॥ नमः स्वस्ति स्वाहा स्वधा जलं वपड् इत्येनेयेगे चतुर्थी विभक्तिभंवति

284

DATIVE CASE.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 16-17.

16. The fourth case-affix is employed in conjunction with the words namah 'salutation,' savasti 'peace,' svāhā, svadhā (terms used in offering oblations to Gods and Pitris respectively), alam 'a match for' 'sufficient for' and vashat a term of oblation.

Ex. नमो देवेभ्यः, स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः, स्वादाऽन्तये, स्वधा पितृभ्यः, अलं नास्ति नास्ताय 'Salutation to Gods'; 'peace to the people'; 'svāhā to fire'; 'svadhā to the Pitris'; 'an athlete is a match for an athlete' &c. The word अलं includes its synonyms also, as प्रभुः, यक्तः &c.; so यपविन्द्राय, यपवन्दे.

The न indicates that the Dative will debar Genitive, in spite of II. 3. 73, in the case of these words, though used benedictively; as स्वस्ति गोप्यैः पूयात् ॥

मध्यकर्मण्यनादरे विभाषाऽप्राशिषु ॥ १७ ॥ पदानि ॥ मध्य-कर्मणि, अनादरे, विभाषा, अप्राशिषु, ( चतुर्थी ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ मध्यकर्मणि प्राशिवर्जिते विभाषा चतुर्थी विभक्ति भंवति अनादरे मध्यमाने ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ पदेतदप्राशिष्विति तदनावादिष्विति वक्तव्यम् ॥

17. In denoting the indirect object, which is not an animal, of the verb manya 'to think,' the dative case is optionally employed, when contempt is to be shown.

Ex. न स्वा तुषं तुषाय वा मध्ये 'I do not consider thee worth a straw.' न स्वा तुषं तुषाय वा मध्ये 'I do not consider thee worth a chaff.' Why do we use the word मध्ये? Observe न स्वा तुषं चिन्तयामि. The optional dative will not be employed with the synonyms of the verb मध्ये. So also the sūtra uses the form मध्ये with the vikaraṇa रूपम्, indicating that it is Divādi that governs a dative, and not the Tanādi न; for the latter governs the accusative only, as न स्वां तुषं मध्ये.

When contempt is not meant, the verb does not govern the Dative, as :—

अन्तमां तुषं मध्ये, मध्ये कापुतुलुतुलुतु । अन्तमायां तुषं मध्ये यद्य माता न पश्यति ॥

'I consider a rock to be a stone, I consider mortar but as wood, I consider him to be the son of a blind woman whose mother cannot see.'

So also when the object of comparison is an animate being, it will not take the dative:—as न स्वां तुषां मध्ये 'I do not consider thee even as a jackal.' The case of न स्वां तुषं मध्ये is an exception.

Vart:—Instead of using अप्राशिषु in the sūtra, the word अनावादिषु should be used. The following words belong to Nāvādi class, they are always in the accusative after the word मध्ये, never in the Dative:—नो 'ship,' काब 'crow,' अन्न 'food,' तुष 'parrot,' and तुषाल 'jackal.'

BK. II. CH. III. § 18-21.]

INSTRUMENTAL CASE.

285

कर्तृ-करणयो स्तृतीया ॥ १८ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्तृ-करणयोः तृतीया ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्तृ-करणयोः क्तृते तृतीया विभक्ति भैति ॥

वार्षिकम् ॥ तृतीया विधाने प्रफुल्लादीनानुपसंख्यानम् ॥

18. In denoting the agent (I. 4. 54) or the instrument (I. 4. 42), the third case-affix is employed.

Ex. देवदत्तेन कृतं 'done by Devadatta,' दानेन श्रुतानि 'he cuts with the sickle.' So also यददत्तेन मुक्तम्, परशुना चिन्तन्ति ॥

Vart:—The following words take the 3rd case. प्रकृति 'original,' प्राय 'almost,' शेष 'gotra,' सम 'equal,' विघ्न 'unequal,' द्विदोष, पंचक and सादृश as प्रायेण वार्षिकः, गार्योऽस्मि शेषेण, सनेन or विषमेण पावति, द्विदोषेनकोशाति &c.

सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने ॥ १९ ॥ पदानि ॥ सहयुक्ते, अप्रधाने (तृतीया) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सहयेन मुक्तेऽप्रधाने तृतीया विभक्तिभैति ॥

19. When the word 'with,' is joined to a word the latter takes the third case, when the sense is that the word in the third case is not the principal but the accompaniment of the principal thing.

Ex. पुत्रेण सहागतः पिता 'the father has come with the son.'

The same will be the result with the synonyms of 'with the son'. So also when the word 'with the son' is understood, as Pāṇini himself uses in I. 2. 65 इद्रो युना &c.

Why do we say 'when not the principal.' Observe, विशेष्य सहेमापाप्य-परशुनोः.

येनाङ्गविकारः ॥ २० ॥ पदानि ॥ येन, अङ्ग-विकार, (तृतीया) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ येनाङ्गेन विकृतेनाङ्गिनो विकारो लभ्यते ततस्तृतीया विभक्ति भैति ॥

20. By whatsoever limb, being defective, is pointed out the defect of the person, after that the third case-affix is employed.

As, अवध्या काणः 'blind of one eye' पादेन लंजः 'lame of foot.' पाशिना कुण्डः &c. The word aṅga in this sūtra applies to the whole body, whatsoever by reason of being a member of the body is defective is indicated here.

इत्यंभूतलक्षणे ॥ २१ ॥ पदानि ॥ इत्यंभूत-लक्षणे, (तृतीया) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कश्चितकारं प्राप्त इत्यंभूत, ललयलवयणित्यं भूतलक्षणे, ततस्तृतीया विभक्ति भैति ॥

2

286

INSTRUMENTAL CASE.

[BK. II. CH. III. § 21-24.]

21. Any mark or attribute, by which is indicated the existence of a particular state or condition, is put in the third case to express this relation.

जटाभिस्तापसः 'he is an ascetic by (the fact of his having) matted hair.'
अपि भवान् कमण्डलुना ह्यापद्मावीत् 'your honor might see the student by the fact of his having a kamandalu.' So also ह्याभिस्तापसः 'a teacher by the fact of having students.'
भिस्तापसः परिज्ञानकम् 'a Parivrājaka by a tuft of hair.' But not so here, कमण्डलुपाशिहालः 'a student has kamandalu in his hand.' Because here in the compound, कमण्डलुपाशि is hidden the mark.

Why do we say ittha-bhuta? Observe बृहं प्रति विद्रोतेन.

संज्ञोऽन्यतरस्यां कर्मणि ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ सम्-श्वः, अन्यतरस्यां, कर्मणि, (तृतीया) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ संज्ञोऽन्यतरस्यां कर्मणि कारके द्वितीयायां प्राप्यायामन्यतरस्यां तृतीया विभक्ति भंवति ॥

22. After the verb sam-jñā the third case-affix is optionally employed in denoting the object.

पिता or पितर संज्ञानीते 'he knows his father.' माता or मातर संज्ञानीते ॥

हेतौ ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ हेतौ, (तृतीया) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कलवाधनयोग्यः पदानि लोके हेतुस्थ्यते; तद्वाचिनस्तृतीया विभक्ति भंवति ॥

23. When a word denotes 'cause,' it takes the third case-affix.

विदाया यशः 'by learning there is produced fame.' धनेन कुलम् 'by wealth, family;' कन्यया शोकः 'by daughter there is grief.'

The word हेतु here is used in its popular sense and not the grammatical hetu (I. 4. 55). Any thing capable of accomplishing a desired object is called hetu.

अकर्तयुंखे पञ्चमी ॥ २४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अकर्तरि, ऋये, पञ्चमी, (हेतौ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्तुर्बर्जितं यदृशं हेतुस्ततः पञ्चमी विभक्ति भंवति ॥

24. A word, implying debt, considered as a 'cause' but not as a kartri or agent, takes the fifth case-affix.

Ex. बताद्वः 'he has been bound on account of a debt of a hundred pieces.'

BK. II. CH. III. § 24-27.]

CASE-AFFIXES.

287

Why do we say 'when not denoting the agent?' Observe यतेन बन्धितः; 'a debt of hundred has thrown him in prison'; here यत being considered as a prayojaka hetu, is an agent and takes the third case-affix.

विभाषा गुणेऽख्रियाम् ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, गुणे, अख्रियाम्, (हेतौ पञ्चमी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गुणे हेतावख्रीलिङ्गे विभाषा पञ्चमी विभक्तिर्भवति ॥

25. The fifth case-affix is employed optionally when the noun expresses an attribute, being the cause of an action, and not being of the feminine gender.

Ex. जाडपने जाडपताम् वा बद्धः 'he has been bound by reason of his dullness.' पांडित्येन वा पांडित्याद् युक्तः 'saved through learning.'

Guṇa-vachana nouns are generally abstract nouns. Therefore not here यतेन कुतम्. If an abstract noun is of feminine gender, this rule will not apply, as युद्ध्या वा प्रध्या युक्तः 'he was set at liberty on account of his skill or wisdom.'

षष्ठी हेतुप्रयोग ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ षष्ठी, हेतु-प्रयोगे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ हेतुप्रग्रहस्य प्रयोगे हेतौ द्रोत्ये षष्ठी विभक्ति भवति ॥

26. The sixth case-affix is employed after a noun implying the cause of an action, when the word hetu is used along with such a word.

Ex. अग्नस्य हेतो भवति 'he dwells for the sake of food.'

सर्वनाम्नस्तृतीया च ॥ २७ ॥ पदानि ॥ सर्वनाम्नः तृतीया, च, (हेतुप्रयोगे) (षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सर्वनाम्नो हेतुप्रग्रहप्रयोगे हेतौ द्रोत्ये तृतीया विभक्ति भवति षष्ठीष ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ निमित्तकारण्डहेतुप् सर्वांसा प्रायदर्थनम् ॥

27. After a sarvanāman (I. 1. 27) when it signifies the cause of an action, and the word hetu is used with it, the third case-affix is employed, as well as the sixth

Ex. कस्य वा केन हेतुना बधति 'for the sake of what does he live?' यस्य वा येन हेतुना बधति ।

Vart:—When the words निमित्त or कारण are so used, almost all the case affixes may be employed; as किं निमित्तं वा केन निमित्तेन वा कस्ये निमित्ताय वा कस्यानिमित्तात् वा कस्य निमित्तस्य वा कस्यिन् निमित्ते बधति. Similarly with

288

ABLATIVE CASE.

BK. II. CH. III. § 27-29.

the words kāraṇa and hetu. Here also the word देवु does not mean the word-form hetu (I. 1. 68) but its synonyms also; as किं मयोजनं or केन मयोजनेन or कले मयोजनाय &c., बधति .

अपादाने पञ्चमी ॥ २८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अपादाने, पञ्चमी ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अपादाने कारणे पञ्चमी विभक्ति भेदति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ पञ्चमीविषाने स्वयजोये कर्मवदुपसंख्यानम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अभिकरते बोपसंख्यानम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ मरणाख्यानयेत्तु पञ्चमी वक्तव्या ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ यत्क्षाध्यकालनिर्माणं तत्र पञ्चमी वक्तव्या ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ तदुत्तारकाले पञ्चमी वक्तव्या ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अच्युतः मयना पञ्चमी च वक्तव्या ॥

28. When the Apādana-kāraka (I. 4. 24) is denoted, the fifth case-affix is employed.

Ex. प्रामादागच्छति 'he comes from the village' (I. 4. 24); युकेन्यो निमेति (I. 4. 25), अध्यवनात् पराजयते (I. 4. 26) &c.

Vart:—The fifth case-affix is employed in denoting the object, when the verbal participle ending in स्वय is elided; as प्रामादागच्छति मेघते = प्रामादात् मेघते 'he sees from a palace.'

Vart:—And under similar circumstances in denoting the location the place where an action is performed is put in the ablative case, as, आपने उपविष्ट मेघते = आपनात् मेघते 'he sees from a seat.'

Vart:—In questions and answers, the fifth case-affix is employed:—कृते भवान्? पाठलिपुनात् 'whence is your Honor coming? From Pataliputra'

Vart:—That point of time or space from which distance in time or space is measured is put in the ablative case:—as, गधीपुनतः यांकार्थं चत्वारि योजनानि 'Sankāśya is from Gavidhuma four yojanas.' कार्तिक्या आग्रदावकी माये 'Agrahāyana is one month from Kārtika. The word denoting the distance in time is put in the locative case, as माये

Vart:—In the above the word denoting the distance in space may be put either in the nominative or locative; as गधीपुनतः यांकार्थं चत्वारि योजनानि or चतुर्थं योजनेषु ।

अन्यारादितरसदिकशब्दाऽचुत्तरपदाजाहियुक्ते ॥ २९ ॥ पदानि ॥

अन्य--आरात्-इतर-ऋते-दिकशब्द-अञ्चु-उत्तरपद-आच्-आहियुक्ते, (पञ्चमी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अन्य आरात् इतर ऋते दिकशब्दाऽचुत्तरपद आच् आहि इत्येतैवेति पञ्चमी विभक्ति भेदति ॥

BK. II. Ch. III. § 29-31.]

GENITIVE CASE.

289

29. When a noun is joined with words meaning 'other than' or with *ārāt* 'near or remote' or *itara* 'different from' or *rite* 'without,' or words indicative of the 'directions' (used also with reference to the time corresponding to them) or with words having *añchu* 'to bend' as the last member of the compound (and expressive of direction), or with words ending with the *affix* *āch* or *āhi* (V. 3. 36 and 37) the fifth case-affix is employed.

Ex. अन्यो, भिन्नो, इतरो, अर्थान्तर, विलम्बो वा देवदत्तात् 'different from Devadatta' आषाढ़ देव दत्तात् 'remote from or near to Devadatta.' The word *ārāt* meaning 'near or remote' would have taken the sixth case-affix by *sūtra* 34, but this enjoins 5th case-affix. ऋते देवदत्तात् 'excepting Devadatta.' द्वैवो ग्रामात् 'east of the village,' उत्तरो ग्रामात् 'north of the village,' द्वैवो ग्रीष्मात् 'the spring is prior to summer' प्राक् प्रत्यग्वा ग्रामात् 'to the east or west of the village' दधिषा दधिषादि वा ग्रामात् 'to the south or in the eastern direction of the village.'

The words like प्राक् &c., formed from the verb *añchu* are also दिक्क्यब्दः; their separate enumeration shows that the sixth case-affix ordained by the next *sūtra* does not come after them.

षष्ट्यतसर्षमत्ययेन ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ षष्टी, अतसर्षमत्ययेन ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अतसर्षमत्ययेन युक्ते षष्टी विभक्ति भैषति ॥

30. The sixth case-affix is employed when used in connection with words ending with affixes having the sense of the *affix* at a such (V. 3. 28).

The *affix* अतसुष् is ordained by V. 3. 28.

Ex. ग्रामस्य दधिषाः उत्तरतः पुरस्तात् उपरि वा 'to the south or north, fore most, in or above the village.'

एनपा द्रवितीया ॥ ३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ एनपा, द्रवितीया ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ एनपञ्चतरस्यामहरे पञ्चष्या इति पश्यति । तेन युक्ते द्वितीया विभक्ति भैषति ॥

31. With a word ending with the *affix* 'enap' (V. 3. 35), the second case-affix is employed as well as the sixth.

Ex. दधिषेन ग्रामम् ग्रामस्य वा 'south of the village.'

290

CASE-AFFIXES.

BK. II. CH. III. § 32-34.

पृथिविनानानाभिस्तृतीयाऽन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ पृथग्-विनः-नानाभिः, तृतीया, अन्यतरस्याम्, (पञ्चमी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पृथक् विना नाना इत्येते योनि तृतीया विभक्ति भैति अन्यतरस्यां पञ्चमी च ॥

32. When joined with the words prithak 'without', vinā 'without' and nānā 'without' the third case-affix is employed, optionally (as well as the fifth and the second).

Ex. रानादानेय रानं वा विना पृथग् नाना वा 'without' or different from Rāma.'

This sūtra may be divided into two parts:—(1) पृथक् विना नानाभिः (2) तृतीयाऽन्यतरस्याम्. By this arrangement we can read dvitiya into the aphorism.

विना वातं विना वधे विद्वत्तुमपत्तनं विना ।

विना इन्ति कृतान्दोषात् केनेनी पातितो द्रुनी ॥

करये च स्तोकाल्पकृच्छुकतिपयस्यासत्त्ववचनस्य ॥ ३३ ॥ पदानि ॥
करये, च, स्तोक-अल्प-कृच्छुकतिपयस्य, असत्त्ववचनस्य, (तृतीया-पञ्चमी-अन्यतरस्यां) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्तोक अल्प कूच्छुकतिपय इत्येतेन्योऽस्त्ववचनेभ्यः करये कारकेऽन्यतरस्यां तृतीया भवति पचे पञ्चमेय ॥

33. When expressing an instrument-kāraka, optionally after the words stoka 'little,' alpa 'little,' kṛichchhra 'difficulty,' and katipaya 'some,' the fifth case-affix is used, when they do not denote material objects.

Ex. स्तोकात् स्तोकेन वा युक्तः and अल्पान्मुक्तः or अल्पेनयुक्तः &c, 'he got off easily &c. But स्तोकेन विपेन इतः, अल्पेन मचुना मचः &c, 'killed by a little poison.' No option allowed, as it qualifies a substance. So also स्तोकं यु चति 'he loosens a little.' Here स्तोक is used as an adverb and not as an instrument (करण).

दूरान्तिकार्यैः षष्ठ्यन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ दूर-अन्ति-क-अर्थैः, षष्ठी, अन्यतरस्याम्, (पञ्चमी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दूरान्तिकार्यैः शब्दैयेनि षष्ठी विभक्तिर्भैति अन्यतरस्यां पञ्चमी च ॥

34. when in conjunction with words having the sense of dūra 'distant,' and antika 'near,' the sixth case-affix is optionally employed.

Ex. ग्रामाद् ग्रामस्य वा वनं दूरं विमुक्तं, अन्तिकं, अभ्याम्, निकटं समीपं वा 'the forest is distant from or near, or to the village.'

BK. II. CH. III. § 34-36.]

CASE-AFFIXES.

291

The force of the word अन्यतरस्वां is to indicate that the 5th case-affix employed in the alternative, would have run into this sūtra, had we not used 'anyatarasyam.'

दूरान्तिकार्थेभ्योद्वितीया च ॥ ३५ ॥ पदायि ॥ दूर-अन्तिक-अर्थेभ्यः, द्वितीया, च, (पञ्चमी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दूरान्तिकार्थेभ्यः शब्देभ्यो द्वितीया विभक्तिर्भवति चकारात्पञ्चमीतुतीयापि यजुच्चीयते ॥

35. After the words having the sense of dūra 'distant,' and antika 'near,' the second case-affix is used as well as the fifth and the third.

Ex. दूरं दूराद् दूरेश वा ग्रामस्य and अन्तिकात्, or अन्तिकेन अन्तिकं ग्रामस्य.

This rule applies only when these words have their original signification and do not denote a substance. Otherwise the proper case-affix should be employed, as दूरः पञ्चाः, दूराय पचे देहि.

सम्भयधिकारये, च, ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ सममी, अधिकरये, च, (दूरान्तिकार्थेभ्यः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सममी विभक्तिर्भवत्यधिकारये कारके चकारा दूरान्तिकार्थेभ्यः ॥

वर्त्तिकम् ॥ सममीविपाने कर्तव्येभ्यपयस्य कर्मयुपसंख्यानम् ॥

वर्त्तिकम् ॥ साध्यसाधुरयोगे च सममी वक्तव्या ॥

वर्त्तिकम् ॥ कारकारार्थार्थं वा कारकत्वे सममी वक्तव्या ॥

वर्त्तिकम् ॥ अकारकारार्थार्थं वा कारकत्वे सममी वक्तव्या ॥

वर्त्तिकम् ॥ तद्विपर्याये च सममी वक्तव्या ॥

वर्त्तिकम् ॥ निमित्तात्कर्मययोगे सममी वक्तव्या ॥

36. The seventh case-affix is employed when the sense is that of location (I. 4. 45) as well as after the words meaning 'distant' or 'near'.

Ex. कटे आस्ते 'he sits on the mat' अन्तिके दूरे वा ग्रामस्य 'near or distant from the village.' स्वास्यां पयति 'he cooks in the pot.' Thus the words दूर and अन्तिक take four case-affixes, namely the second, third, fifth and seventh.

*Vart*:—Words like अभीतिन् 'who has learnt,' पृथ्वीतिन् 'who has comprehended,' *i. e.*, words formed by adding द्वन्द्व to the past participle in च, govern the locative of that which forms their object:—as अभीति व्याकरणे 'versed in grammar,' परिगणिती यश्चिके 'well versed in sacrificial rites,' आङ्ग्रान्ती द्वन्द्वि 'well read in the Veda.' See V. 2. 88.

292

CASE-AFFIXES.

[BK. III. CH. II. § 36-38.]

Vart:—The words बापु and अवापु govern the locative of that towards whom goodness or otherwise is shown; as नातिरे बापुसापु वा 'well behaved or ill-behaved towards his mother.'

Vart:—The Locative absolute is used in cases other than those specified in the next sūtra, namely, in cases where the action done or suffered does not indicate the time of another action; as अङ्गु भुञ्जानेपु दरिद्रा आसते 'the poor are sitting, while the rich are eating,' दरिद्रेपु आसीनेपु अङ्गुभुजते 'the rich are eating, while the poor being seated.' So also vice versa.

Vart:—The Locative is sometimes used to denote the object or purpose for which anything is done; as.

चर्मणि द्वीपिनं इति, इतयोर्दन्तिकु लब्धः ।

केषेपु चमरीं इति योहि पुष्कलको हतः ॥

'Man kills the tiger for his skin, the elephant for his tusks, for chamari cow for her hair, and the musk-deer for its musk.'

यस्य च भावेन भावलक्ष्याम् ॥ ३७ ॥ पदानि ॥ यस्य, च, भावेन, भाव-लक्ष्याम्, ( सप्तमी ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ भावः क्रिया यस्य च भावेन यस्य च क्रियाक्रियान्तरं लभ्यते ततो भाववतः सप्तमी विभक्तिभेदति ॥

37. By the action (bhāva) of whatsoever, the time of another action is indicated, that takes the seventh case-affix.

This is Locative Absolute. गोपु हृदयनानापु गतः 'the cows being milked, he went away' दुग्धारवागतः 'and returned when they were milked' अग्निपु दुग्धानेपु गतः, दुग्धानापतः.

Why do we say 'by the action of whatsoever'? Observe यो नटाभिः च भुक्ते. Why have we used the word 'action' twice? Witness यो 'भुक्ते' च देवदत्तः.

षष्ठी घानादरे ॥ ३८ ॥ पदानि ॥ षष्ठी, च, अन् आदरे, ( सप्तमी, भावेन भावलक्ष्याम् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अनादराधिके भावलक्ष्ये भाववतः षष्ठीयसन्धौ विभक्ती भवतः ॥

38. The sixth case-affix is employed (as well as the seventh), when disregard is to be shown, after that by whose action the time of another action is indicated.

This is Genitive Absolute. पदतः पदतिथा प्राज्ञानीम् 'in spite of her weeping, he went away.' The force of this genitive is that of the English word 'not-withstanding' 'in spite of' 'for all,' &c., नन्दाः पञ्च इद इता: पञ्चतो राघवश्च 'the

BK. II. CH. III. § 38-41.]

GENITIVE CASE.

293

Nandas were killed like so many beasts Rakshasa looking on,' (not-with-standing that Rakshasa was looking on).

स्वामिश्वराधिपतिदायादसाक्षिप्रतिभूप्रसूतैश्च ॥ ३९ ॥ पदानि ॥
स्वामिन्-ईश्वर-अधिपति-दायाद-साक्षिन्-प्रतिभू-प्रसूतैः, च, (षष्ठी सप्तमी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ स्वामिन् ईश्वर अधिपति दायाद साक्षिन् प्रतिभू प्रसूत इत्येतैयेने षष्ठी सप्तमी विभक्तीभवतः ॥

39. The sixth and the seventh case-affixes are used after words when they are joined with svāmin 'master,' īśvara 'lord,' adhipati 'ruler,' dāyāda 'an heir,' sākshin 'witness,' pratibhū 'a surety,' and prasūta 'begotten'.

नवां नोपु वा स्वामी or ईश्वर 'master of cows' So also नवावधिपतिः or नोपुवधिपतिः, नवां दायादः or नोपु दायादः, नवां or नोपु वाणी प्रविष्टः &c.

These words naturally would have governed the Genitive; the present sūtra ordains Locative as well.

आयुकृतकुशलाभ्यां चासेवायाम् ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ आयुकृत-कुशलाभ्यां, च, चासेवायाम्, (षष्ठी सप्तमी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आयुक्तो व्यापारितः कुशलो निपुणः लाभ्यां योगे आसेवायां गन्धमानायां षष्ठी सप्तमी विभक्तीभवतः ॥

40. In conjunction with the words āyukta 'engaged,' and kuśala 'skilful,' when meaning entire absorption in an engagement, the sixth and the seventh case-affixes are used after a word.

Ex. आयुक्तः कुशलो वा कटकरये कटकरयस्य वा 'deeply absorbed in mat-making.'

When not meaning 'deeply absorbed,' the construction is different; as आयुक्तो नः प्रकटे 'the cow is slightly yoked to the cart.' Here the seventh case-affix only is employed.

यतश्च निर्द्वारेषाम् ॥ ४१ ॥ पदानि ॥ यतः, च, निर्द्वारेषाम्, (षष्ठी-सप्तमी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यतो निर्द्वारेष ततः षष्ठीसप्तमी विभक्तीभवतः ॥

41. The sixth and the seventh case-affixes are used after those words from which specification is made, (as of an individual from the whole class).

3

294

CASE AFFIXES.

[BK. II. CH. III. § 41-44.

Ex. गवां गोयु वा कृष्णा बहुवीराः 'among cows the black one gives much milk; मनुष्याणां or मनुष्येषु छत्रियः सुरतनः.'

A nirdhāraṇa or specification is made by separating one from the many by reason of its genus, quality and action (II. 2. 10).

पञ्चमी विभक्ते ॥ ४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ पञ्चमी, विभक्ते, ( यतय निद्रारूपम् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यत्पिन्तिद्रारूपञ्चये विभक्तमस्ति ततः पञ्चमी विभक्तिभवति ॥ विभागो विभक्तं ॥

42. The fifth case-affix is employed when the thing specified is different or divided from (and not included in) that from which specification is intended.

This debars the sixth and the seventh case-affixes, as, नाथुराः पाठलि-पुनःशुक्लारताराः 'Mathura is more beautiful than Pāṭaliputra.'

साधुनिपुणीभ्यामचर्यां सप्तम्यमतेः ॥ ४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ साधु-निपुणाभ्यां, अचर्यं, सप्तमी-अप्रतेः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ साधु निपुण इत्येताभ्यां योगेऽचर्यां मध्यमानायां सप्तमी विभक्तिभवति न चेत्, प्रतिः प्रयुज्यते ॥

43. In conjunction with the words sādhu 'good,' and nipuna 'skillful,' when they denote respect, the seventh case-affix is employed; provided that the word prati is not used.

नातरि साधुः or निपुणः 'good behaved towards his mother'? But साधुदेवदत्तो नातरं प्रति 'Devadatta is good behaved towards his mother.'

Why do we say 'when respect is denoted'? Observe, साधुर्द्व्योराधः 'the servant is good towards the king. Here it is a bare statement of a fact.

The exception applies not only to प्रति but to other prepositions, like परि, ऋतु &c., as, नातरं परि साधुदेवदत्तः ॥

प्रसितोत्सुकाभ्यां तृतीया च, ॥ ४४ ॥ पदानि ॥ प्रसित-उत्सुकाभ्यां, तृतीया, च, ( सप्तमी ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रसित उत्सुक इत्येताभ्यां योगे तृतीया विभक्तिभवति चकारात्सप्तमी च ॥

44. In conjunction with the words prasita 'longing for,' and utsuka 'greatly desirous of,' the third case-affix is used after a word, as well as the seventh.

Ex. निद्रायां निद्रया वा उत्सुकः 'longing for sleep.' केयैः शकेयेषु प्रसितः

BK. II. CH. III. § 45-47.]

CASE-AFFIXES.

295

नक्षत्रे च लुपि ॥ ४५ पदानि ॥ नक्षत्रे, च, लुपि, (तृतीया सप्तमी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लुबन्तान्नवत्रयन्दात् तृतीयासप्तम्यो विभक्ती भवतः ॥

45. When an affix declaring the time of an Asterism is elided by lup (IV. 2. 4); the seventh and the third case-affixes are used after the word, whose affix is so elided.

Ex. पुण्ये पुण्ये वा पायसम्पन्नीयात् 'when the moon is in the Asterism of Pushya, let him drink milk.' See Rules IV. 2. 4 and IV 2. 5. So also नयाभिः पललीदनं नयालु पललीदनम्. But not so here पंचालेषु वसन्ति 'he lives in Panchāla'. Here the country is meant, and not a star, though here also there is elision of the Taddhita affix.

Why do we say 'lup elision'? Observe नयालु ग्रहः 'the planet in the Maghā.' Here there is no elision. But why not in अद्वापुष्यः, अद्वाकृतिका. Because they do not denote location, which is understood. It is when location is expressed by such words that we may use the third case-affix in the alternative.

प्रातपादिकार्थलिङ्गपरिमाणवचन मात्रे प्रथमा ॥ ४६ ॥ पदानि ॥
प्रातिपदिक-अर्थ-लिङ्ग-परिमाण-वचन-मात्रे, प्रथमा ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रातिपदिकार्थमात्रे लिङ्गमात्रे परिमाणमात्रे वचनमात्रे प्रथमा विभक्तिभवति ॥

46. Where the sense is that of the Nominalstem (I. 2. 45) or of gender only, or measure only or number only, the first case-affix is employed.

Ex. उच्चैः 'aloft,' नीचैः 'below,' कुमारी 'virgin,' वृशः 'tree,' कूर्म 'owl,' द्रोणः 'a measure'. By 'number' grammatical number is meant; as एकः 'one,' द्वौ 'two,' बहवः 'many'.

The sense of a Prātipadika is to denote mere existence. Genders are three, masculine, feminine and neuter. Measures are such as drōpa, khāri, ādhaka &c. Numbers are singular, dual and plural. The Nipatas which do not denote anything are also Prātipadika.

संशोधने च ॥ ४७ ॥ पदानि ॥ संशोधने, च (प्रथमा) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ संशोधने च प्रथमा विभक्तिभवति ॥

47. And when the sense is that of addressing, the first case-affix is employed.

Ex. दे राम 'O Ram' दे रामो, दे रामाः ॥

VOCATIVE CASE.

[BK. II. CH. III. § 48-51.]

साऽऽमन्त्रितम् ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ सआमन्त्रिम् (सन्नोधने प्रथमा) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ संबोधने वा प्रथमा तदन्तं शब्दरूपनामन्त्रितसंभवति ॥

48. The word ending with the first case-affix, in the sense of addressing, is called Amantrita or vocative (VIII. 2. 78).

एकवचनं संबुद्धिः ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ एकवचनं सम्बुद्धिः, (आमन्त्रितम् प्रथ०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आमन्त्रितप्रथमाया यदेकवचनं तत्संबुद्धिसंबंधं भवति ॥

49. In the sense of vocative, the singular number of the first case-affix is called Sambuddhi.

The vocative singular is called sambuddhi, when it is employed in the vocation. Thus VI. 1. 69 declares 'after an inflection base ending in एक or in a short vowel, a consonant is elided if it be that of Sambuddhi' as दे राम ॥

षष्ठी शेषे ॥ ५० ॥ पदानि ॥ षष्ठी, शेषे ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कर्मादिभ्योऽन्यः प्रातिपदिकार्यव्यतिरिक्तः स्वस्वामिसंबन्धादिः शेषस्तत्र षष्ठी विभक्तिमेवति ॥

50. The sixth case-affix is employed in the remaining case, that is to say, where there is a sense, such as the relation between property and its owner, &c. different from that of a Nominal-stem.

Ex. राधः पुरुषः 'the king's man' पशोः पादः 'beast's foot' पितुः पुत्रः father's son.'

शोऽविदर्थस्य करणे ॥ ५१ ॥ पदानि ॥ शः, अविदर्थस्य, करणे, (षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आनातेरविदर्थस्याधानार्थस्य करणे कारके षष्ठी विभक्तिमेवति ॥

51. Of the verb वा jñā, when not used in the sense of 'to know,' the instrument takes the sixth case-affix.

Ex. मधुगे जानोते 'he engages in sacrifice with honey'. So also सर्पिषे जानोते. The verb वा when not meaning 'to know', has the significance of
