'to act, or to engage in;' or it may denote 'false knowledge'; as बधिरि रक्खः प्रतिहतावा. Compare I. 3. 45.

But not so here स्वरेण पुत्रं जानाति 'he recognises the son by the voice.'

अधीगर्थदेयेशांकर्मणि ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अधि-इक-अर्थ-दय-ईशां, कर्मणि, (षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अधीगर्थाः स्वरसायाः । दय दानगतिस्वशेष । ईश रेख्यर्थ । एतेषां कर्मणि कारणे शेषत्वेन विवक्षितं षष्ठी विभक्ति भंवति ॥

52. Of the verbs having the sense of 'remembering,' (adhik) and of day 'to give,' 'to pity' 'to protect,' to move,' and of isā 'to rule or be master of,' the object takes the sixth case-affix.

Ex. भातुः अभ्येति 'he remembers the mother,' बधिरि दयते 'he gives clarified butter,' भायं भात्रायामीष्टे 'he can not rule his limbs.' But not so here भातुः ईशः स्वरति because युग here is not the object. The word शेष is also understood here. So that the cases not otherwise provided for, take this case. So that भातः स्वरति is also allowed.

कृत्रः प्रतियत्ने ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ कृत्रः, प्रतियत्ने, (कर्मणि शेषे षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ करोतः कर्मणि कारणे शेषत्वेन विवक्षितं प्रतियत्ने गन्धमाने षष्ठी विभक्ति भंवति ॥

53. The object of the verb krī takes the sixth case-affix, when it means 'to impart a new quality or virtue (I. 3. 32).

Ex. शेषादकस्योपस्कृते 'the wood gives a new quality to the water' (or he prepares the wood and water for sacrifice). (By VI. 1. 139, च is inserted).

When प्रतियत is not meant, the second case-affix is employed: as कर्त करोति.

The word शेष is also understood here. So that we have also शेषादकस्य पस्कृते ॥

रुजार्थानां भाववचनानामज्वरे ॥ ५४ ॥ पदानि ॥ रुज-अर्थानां, भाववचनानाम्, अज्वरे, (कर्मणि शेषे षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ रुजार्थानां भातुः भाववचनानां भावकर्तृकारां स्वरिवर्जितानां कर्मणि कारणे शेषत्वेन विवक्षितं षष्ठी विभक्ति भंवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अज्वरि संताप्योरिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

298

GENITIVE CASE.

[BK. II. CH. III. § 54-56.

54. The object of verbs having the sense of *ruj* 'to afflict', with the exception of the Causative verb *jvaraya* 'to be feverish,' takes the sixth case-affix, when the verb expresses a condition (*i. e.*, when the subject is an Abstract noun).

Ex. चौरस्य बजति रोगः 'the disease afflicts the chief' चौरस्यावयति आनयः ।

Why do we say 'when the subject is an Abstract noun'? Observe नद्यो कुलानि बजति 'the river breaks the banks.' So also not here चौरं ज्वरयति ज्वरः 'the fever burns the thief.' So also when the verb संताप is used, चौरं संतापयति तापः ।

The word शेष is also understood here. Thus चौरं बजति रोगः ॥

आशिषि नाथः ॥ ५५ ॥ पदानि ॥ आशिषि, नाथः ( कर्मणि शेषे षष्ठी ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नाथं नाथं याज्ञोपतायैश्वर्याधोऽप्यु पठ्यते, तस्याधिः क्रियस्य कर्मणि कारके शेष शेषेण विवक्षिते षष्ठी विभक्ति भयति ॥

55. Of the verb *nāth* when meaning 'to bless'; the object takes the sixth case-affix.

Ex. नपुने नागते 'he blesses the honey.' But नायवकथुपनायति, अंन पुनी-कापीश्च 'he solicits mânavaka saying (child) son, study.' Here नाय does not mean to bless, and so it takes the accusative case.

जासिनिम्रहणनाटकाथपिषां हिंसायाम् ॥ ५६ ॥ पदानि ॥ जासि-निम्रहण-नाट-काथ-पिषां, हिंसायाम्, ( कर्मणि षष्ठी ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जासि निम्रहण नाट काथ पिषु हरयेतेषां चाहनां, हिंसा क्रियायां कर्मणि कारके षष्ठी विभक्ति भयति ॥

56. The object of the verbs *jāsi* 'to strike'; 'to hurt,' *han* 'to strike' preceded by नि and म, *nāt* 'to injure,' 'krāth,' and 'pish,' when they mean, 'to injure,' takes the sixth case-affix.

चौरस्य योज्ञावयति, निम्रहन्ति, निहन्ति, प्रहन्ति, प्रबिहन्ति, उन्नाटयति, काययति, पिनहि वा, 'he injures the thief.'

The root *कथु* belonging to the Churadi class should be taken, and not *Divādi*. इन with the prepositions *pra* and *ni* may be taken in any order. The root *कथु* takes in the causative *vriddhi* irregularly. The verb is *Bhvādi* and falls into the subdivision *ghatādi*, and is called there a *निम्ह* verb; all *निम्ह* verbs shorten their penultimate before the causative *affix* *विषु* (VI. 4. 92). Thus *कथु* is an irregularity.

BK. II. CH. III. § 56-59.]

GENITIVE CASE.

299

Why do we say 'when meaning to injure'? Observe घाना: पिन्हि 'he pounds the barley.'

The word शेष is also understood here as चीरभुजाययति. Only these govern the genitive, not so here चीरं दिनन्ति, चीरं विदन्ति ॥

व्यवहूपशोः समर्थयोः ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ व्यवहू-पशोः, समर्थयोः (कर्मणि षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ व्यवहू पशु इत्येतयोः समर्थयोः समानार्थयोः कर्मणि कारके षष्ठी विभक्तिभवति ॥

57. The object of the verbs vyavahri and pan when they are synonymous, that is when they mean 'dealing in sale and purchase transactions' or 'staking in gambling,' takes the sixth case-affix.

Ex. मतस्य व्यवहरति or पशते 'he deals in, or stakes hundred.'

Why does not the verb पशु take the affix जावू? It takes जावू when meaning 'to praise or honor,' and not in the sense of 'gambling, or bartering' &c. Not so here मतानां व्यवहरति 'he throws the dice,' ब्राह्मणाद् पश्यते 'he praises the Brāhmaṇas.' The word शेष is also here understood, so that we have मतं पशते 'he stakes a hundred.'

दिवस्तदर्थस्य ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ दिवः, तदर्थस्य । (व्यवहूपशोः समर्थयोः कर्मषष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ व्यवहूपशिसमानार्थस्य दीज्यते कर्मणि षष्ठी विभक्तिभवति ॥

58. The object of the verb div when having the above-mentioned sense of 'dealing' or 'staking,' takes the sixth case-affix.

Ex. मतस्य दीज्यति 'he stakes or deals in a hundred.' But not in ब्राह्मणं दीज्यति 'he jokes with the Brahmana.'

The yoga vibhāga when this root might well have been included in the last aphorism, is for the sake of the succeeding sūtras, in which the anuvṛ itti of दिव runs, and not of others.

विभाषोपसर्गे ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, उपसर्गे, (दिवस्तदर्थस्य कर्मणि षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपसर्गे सति दिवस्तदर्थस्य कर्मणि कारके षष्ठी विभक्तिभवति ॥

59. The object of the verb div when having the above-mentioned sense of dealing or staking, optionally takes the sixth case-affix, when it is preceded by an upasarga (or pre-position).

302

GENITIVE CASE

[BK. II. CH. III. § 64-66.]

location is not meant: as द्विरुद्दीनो बु'के. The शेष being understood we have द्विरुद्दीनो.

कर्तृ-कर्मणोः कृति ॥ ६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ कर्तृ-कर्मणोः, कृति ।
(षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कृत्स्नयोगे कर्तरि कर्मणि च षष्ठी विभक्तिभवति ॥

65. The sixth case affix is employed after a word, in denoting the agent and the object, when used along with a word ending with a krit affix (III. 1.93).

Ex. क्रियां कालिदासस्य 'the composition of Kālidāsa.' आदाता कृतज्ञां 'the performer of sacrifice.' So also भवतः आर्यिका 'your turn of lying down.' अपां खट्टा, पुरां भेत्ता वज्रस्य भर्त्ती. But not in शत्रुघ्नभेत्ता 'cutting with weapon.'

Why do we say 'krit?' Not so when a Taddhita-affix is employed as कृतज्ञवाकर्त्ती. In other words, the genitive in Sanskrit is both subjective and objective.

उभयप्राप्तौ कर्मणि ॥ ६६ ॥ उभयप्राप्तौ, कर्मणि, (कृति षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उभयोः प्राप्निर्ध्वस्मिन्कृति शेषभुवयप्राप्तिस्तत्कर्मणयेय षष्ठी विभक्तिभवति, न कर्तरि ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अकाकारयोः स्त्री प्रत्यययोः प्रयोगे नेति वक्तव्यम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ शेषे विभाषा ॥

66. When the agent and the object of the action denoted by the words formed by krit-affixes, are both used in a sentence, in the object only, the sixth case-affix is employed, and not in the agent (the object is put in the genitive case and not the agent).

आद्यव्ये गवां दोहोऽगोपालकेन 'the milking of a cow without a cowherd is a wonder.' रोषते मे योदनस्य भोजनं देवदत्तेन. 'The eating of rice by Devadatta pleases me;' पवनः पारं पवनदत्तेन 'the drinking of milk by Yajñadatta.'

Vart:—'When the agent and object are both used, the agent is put in the instrumental, or genitive case, when, as some say, the krit terminations are of the feminine gender, or as others say, when the terminations are of any gender; as, विचित्रा जगतः कृतिश्रेणिरिचा वा 'the creation of the world by Hari is wonderful.' शब्दानामुद्रावसनाचार्येण आचार्यस्यवा 'the dissertation on words by the āchārya' बन्धिवादि सूक्ष्म्य कृतिः पाणिनेः or पाणिनिना 'beautiful is the structure of sūtra by Pāṇini.' Apte.

कृतस्य च, वर्त्तमाने ॥ ६७ ॥ पदानि ॥ कृतस्य, च, वर्त्तमाने
(षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कस्य वर्त्तमानकालविहितस्य प्रयोगे षष्ठी विभक्तिभवति ॥

BK. II. CH. III. § 67-69.]

CASE-AFFIX.

303

वार्तिकम् ॥ नृपुं सके भावउपसंख्यानम् ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ श्रेयविधानात् सिद्धम् ॥

67. The past participle ending in क when used in the sense of the present tense, (III. 2. 187 and 188) is used with the genitive.

Ex. राधां प्रजितः 'honored by kings,' अज्ञेयमते महिषते: 'I alone am regarded by the king.'

Why do we say 'क'? Observe ओदनं पचनान: 'rice is cooked.' Why do we say 'when denoting the present tense'? Observe ग्रामं गत: 'gone to the village.'

Vart:—When used as abstract neuter nouns, past participles are used with the genitive, as नृपुं सखं नृपुं 'the dancing of a peacock' 'बालस्य हसितं' 'the laughing of the student', कोकिलस्य व्याहृतम् 'the screaming of the cuckoo.' When, however, agent is desired to be particularised, the instrumental case is employed: as काश्य हसितम्.

This sutra debars sutra 69 by which genitive is prohibited after Nishthā affixes. This is an exception to that sutra.

अधिकरणवाचिनश्च ॥ ६८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अधिकरणवाचिनः, च, (षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कोधिकरणे चेति बधयति तस्य प्रयोगे षष्ठी विभक्तिभवति ॥

68. The past participle in क is used with the genitive when the former expresses location (III. 4. 76).

This also is an exception to the prohibition about Nishthā contained in II. 3. 69. As इदेनेयानासितम् 'this is their seat.' इदेनेयां प्रथितं 'this is their sleeping.'

In connection with verbs taking two objects, both take the genitive case, when a word ending in krit-affix denotes the agent, as they would have taken the accusative: as, नेताऽश्वस्य ग्रामस्य चैत्रः 'Chaitra is the leader of the horse of the village.' When, however, one is the principal, then the object takes the genitive: as, नेताऽश्वस्य ग्रामं चैत्रः, 'Chaitra leads the horse to the village.'

न लोकाव्ययनिष्ठाखलयंतूनाम् ॥ ६९ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, ल-उ-उक-अव्यय-निष्ठा-खलय-तूनाम्, (षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ल उ उक अव्यय निष्ठा खलयं तृपुं इत्येतेषां प्रयोगे षष्ठी विभक्ति नं भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ उक प्रतिवेधे कनेर्मायायामप्रतिषेधः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अव्ययप्रतिषेधे तेष्वत्कृपुनोऽप्रतिषेधः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ द्विषः श्रुत्वा वचनम् ॥

304

CASE-AFFIXES.

[Bk. II. Ch. III. § 69-70.

69. The sixth case-affix is not used to express the agent or the object, when the word is governed by an Active Participle ending in the affix ख, or ख, or खक, or by an Indeclinable, or by a Past Participle in ख and खब्बु, or by a word ending in an affix having the sense of खल् or by a Noun of agency formed by खुन् ॥

After these words, the Instrumental case must be employed to denote the Agent, and the Accusative case to denote the object. This *sūtra* debars Genitive which would have come by II. 3. 65. The word खाक is formed by ख+ख+ख=ख+खक=खाक.

1. The word ख means the substitutes of ख *i.e.*, the Present Participles in खब्बु, खाब्बु (III. 2. 124), खब्बु (III. 2. 106) खब्बु (III. 2. 107) खि and खिब् (III. 2. 172). Thus खोदनं खब्बु, खब्बानः, खब्बानः or खब्बिबाब्, खब्बिः खब्बिबब्, खब्बिनिः ॥

2. The affix ख is enjoined by III. 2. 168, as, खटं खिकिबु, खोदनं खुब्बु ॥ The prohibition applies when a word ending in खब्बुब्बु (III. 2. 136) is the governing term; as, खब्बाबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु ॥

3. The affix खक is ordained by III. 2. 154: as खब्बाबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु ॥

*Vart*:— But the word खाब्बुक in the classical Sanskrit, governs the Genitive, as खब्बाबब्बु 'lusting for the slave.'

4. Indeclinables formed by खुन् affixes, as, खटं खुब्बा, खोदनं खुब्बा ॥

*Vart*:— This prohibition, however, does not apply to the indeclinables formed by खब्बुब (III. 4. 16) and खब्बुब (III. 4. 17), as, खुब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु (I. 1. 40).

5. Nishṭhā *i.e.*, ख and खब्बु; as खोदनं खुब्बाबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु.

6. The words formed by खब्बिबब्बु affixes (III. 3. 126), as, खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु.

7. The खुन् in the aphorism is a pratyāhāra, formed by taking the खु of खब्बु (III. 2. 129) and the final खु of खुब्बु (III. 2. 135), meaning the affixes खब्बिबब्बु (III. 2. 128), खब्बिबब्बु (III. 2. 129), खब्बिबब्बु (III. 2. 130) and खुब्बु (III. 2. 135). As खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु, खब्बिबब्बु, खब्बिबब्बु, खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु

*Vart*:— Optionally so, when the root खिब् takes the affix खब्बु, as, खब्बिबब्बु or खब्बिबब्बु खब्बिबब्बु ॥

अक्रेनोभविष्यदाधमगययोः ॥ ९० ॥ पदानि ॥ अक-इनोः, भविष्यद्व-आधमगययोः ( षष्ठी ) ॥

युनिः ॥ अकस्य भविष्यति खाले खिब्बिरस्येनस्तु भविष्यति खाधमगययें च खिब्बिरस्य प्रयोगे षष्ठी खिमखिनं भवति ॥

BK. II. CH. III. § 70-72.]

CASE-AFFIXES.

305

70. The sixth case-affix is not used when the word is governed by a verbal noun in अः denoting futurity, or in इह denoting 'futurity and indebtedness.'

The affix अः, such as रतुल, युज् &c., denote futurity, and never denote indebtedness. The affix इह such as शिनि (III. 3. 3 and 170) denotes both. Thus कटं कारको युजति 'he goes to make a mat.' ओदां भोजको युजति 'he goes to eat rice.' So also with इह, as ग्रामं गनी 'he has to go to the village.' इहं दानी 'he owes hundred.'

Why do we say 'when denoting futurity or indebtedness'? Observe बबानां लाबकः 'the cutter of barley.' यतूनां पावकः, अवश्यं करी कटस्थः ॥

Why is the Genitive employed in the following ययंबतस्य गुरकः, युजपीलानां दयकः? The words गुरक and दयक, though formed by अः (III. 1. 133), are not formed by that अः which denotes futurity, viz., III. 3. 10. The present sūtra relates to this latter अः, and not every अः in general.

कृत्यानां कर्तरि वा ॥ ७१ ॥ पदानि ॥ कृत्यानां, कर्तरि, वा, (षष्ठी) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ कृत्यानां प्रयोगे कर्तरि वा षष्ठी विभक्तिभवति, न कर्तरि ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ उभयमासी कृत्ये षष्ठ्या प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

71. The sixth case-affix is optionally employed in denoting the agent, (but not the object), when the word is governed by a Future Passive Participle (kritya).

By II. 3. 65, verbal nouns, (krit-formed), always govern the Genitive in denoting agent or object. The present sūtra declares an option as to agent only, in the case of those verbal nouns which are Future Passive Participles. Thus भवतः or भवता कटः कर्तव्यः (III. 1. 95).

Why do we say 'in denoting the agent'? In denoting the object, no option is allowed; the Genitive is compulsory. As गेयो मानवकः साङ्ग्रान् ॥

Vart:—The prohibition of the Genitive should be stated in the case of the Future Passive Participles of those verbs which govern two objects. Thus कष्टव्या ग्रामं गाला देवदत्तेन, नेतव्या ग्राममजा देवदत्तेन ॥

तुल्याधैरतुलोपमाभ्यां तृतीयाऽन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ७२ ॥ पदानि ॥
तुल्य-अर्थैः, अतुल-उपमाभ्यां, तृतीया, अन्यतरस्याम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तुल्यार्थैः शब्दयोगे तृतीया विभक्तिभवत्यन्यतरस्यां, पचे षष्ठी च, तुलोपमा शब्दो बभेचित्वा ॥

72. The third or the sixth case-affix may optionally be employed, when the word is joined with another word meaning 'like to or resemblance'; excepting तुलां and उपमा

306

CASE-AFFIXES.

[BK. II. CH. III. § 72-73.]

Thus तुल्यो देवदत्तेन or देवदत्तस्य, गद्गुरो देवदत्तेन, or देवदत्तस्य ॥ But with तुला and उपमा the Genitive must necessarily be employed. As तुला देवदत्तस्य नास्ति, उपमा कृष्णस्य न विदाते ॥

Though the anuvritti of वा was understood in this sūtra from the previous sūtra, yet the repetition of अन्यतरस्यात् is for the sake of the subsequent sūtra. The word च in II. 3. 73 attracts the word अन्यतरस्यात् into that sūtra; but had the word अन्यतरस्यात् not been used in this sūtra, then the word च would have attracted the word तृतीया instead, which is not desired.

On this sūtra, Professor Apte says:—'Pānini says that the words तुला and उपमा can not be used with the Instrumental. But this is against good usage: as. तुलां, यदादोहितं दंतवाससा (Kum. Sam. V. 24), नमसा तुलां समादरोह (Raghuvamsa VIII. 15). स्कुटोपसं भूतिवितेन यंभुना (Māgh I. 4).'

चतुर्थी चाशिष्यायुण्यमद्रभद्रकुशलसुखार्थहितैः ॥ ७३ ॥ पदानि ॥
चतुर्थी, च, आशिषि, आयुष्य-मद्र-भद्र-कुशल-सुख-अर्थ-हितैः, (अन्यतर-स्याम्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ आशिषि गन्धमानावान् आयुष्य मद्र भद्र कुशल सुख अर्थ हित इत्येतैवेति चतुर्थी विभक्तिर्यति । चकारो विकल्पानुकर्षणार्थः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अनायुष्यादीनां पर्यायैश्वर्यं कर्तव्यम् ॥

73. The fourth as well as the sixth case-affix may be employed, when blessing is intended in connection with the words āyusha 'long life,' madra 'joy,' bhadra 'good fortune,' kuśala 'welfare,' sukha 'happiness,' artha 'prosperity,' and hita 'good.'

The च in the sūtra makes the employment of Dative optional: in the alternative we have Genitive.

Vari:—In this sūtra आयुष्य &c., include their synonyms also.

Thus आयुष्य देवदत्ताय भूयात् or आयुष्य देवदत्तस्य भूयात् ॥ Similarly चिरं जीवितं, भद्रं, भद्रं, कुशलं, निरानयं, सुखं, शं, अयौ, प्रयोजनं, हितं पश्य देवदत्ताय or देवदत्तस्य भूयात् ॥

Why do we say when 'benediction is intended'? Observe आयुष्य देवदत्तस्य तपः 'the austerity is the cause of the long life of Devadatta.' Here there is no option allowed: and the Genitive case is only employed.

ॐ

## ॥ द्वितीयाध्यायस्य चतुर्थः पादः ॥

### BOOK II.

#### CHAPTER IV.

द्विगुरेकवचनम् ॥ १ ॥ पदानि ॥ द्विगुः । एक-वचनम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ द्विगुः समासः एकवचनं भवति ॥

1. The compound Dvigu (II. 1. 52) is singular in number.

The word एकवचन is a genitive Tat-purusha compound meaning 'the expression for one,' that is to say, it expresses the sense of unity. The rule therefore, enjoins that the sense inherent in a Dvigu compound is that of unity.

This is confined to Samāhāra Dvigu *i. e.*, an aggregate compound taken in a collective sense. As, पञ्चवर्ण 'an aggregate of five cows,' पञ्चवर्ण (IV. 1. 21.). The sense of Dvigu being that of one, it follows that it retains the singular number even when further modified by other affixes, and used as an attributive and though no longer a Dvigu; as, पञ्चवर्णीयं योनना ॥

द्वन्द्वश्च प्राखितूर्यसेनाङ्गनाम् ॥ २ ॥ पदानि ॥ द्वन्द्वः, च, प्राखि-
तूर्य-सेना-अङ्गनाम् ( एकवचनं ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ प्रायङ्गनां द्वन्द्व एकवचनम्, तथातूर्यङ्गनां सेनाङ्गनां च ॥

2. A Dvandva compound too is singular in number, when it is compounded of words signifying members of the animal body, players (or singers or dancers) and component parts of an army.

As, पाश्चिपादम् 'the hand and foot' धिरेत्तीवं 'the head and neck' चार्ङ्गिरुपाश्चित्रम् 'players on the mridanga and panava (kinds of drums)' रथिकादवरोहम् 'the soldiers on chariot and horse,' बीजादाकपरिवादम्, रथिक-
पादातम् ॥

This rule applies to cases of Samāhāra Dvandva or aggregate Dvandva Compounds only; and not to Haratara Dvandva (II. 2. 29.)

308

DVANDVA COMPOUND.

[BK. II. CH. IV. § 2-3.

In the Dvandva Compounds of animals such as elephants, horses, &c., the singular is optional; (II. 4. 12.) The present rule also gives us an index as to where we must make Samāhāra Dvandva and where an Itaretara Dvandva. The Dvandva compounds of words signifying members of animal body, players or army, are always and solely Samāhāra Dvandva. The compounds of words like दधिपथी 'curd and milk' (II. 4. 14.) are purely Itaretara Dvandva and can never be Samāhāra Dvandva; while compounds of words denoting tree, animals &c., (II. 4. 12.) are optionally either Samāhāra or Itaretara Dvandva.

अनुवादे चरणानाम् ॥ ३ ॥ पदानि ॥ अनुवादे, चरणानाम् ।
( द्वन्द्वः, एकवचनम् )

वृत्तिः ॥ चरणानां द्वन्द्व एकवद्भवति अनुवादे गन्धमाने ॥
वार्तिकम् ॥ स्थेयोर्द्वन्द्वन्वां चेति वक्तव्यम् ॥

3. A Dvandva compound of words signifying persons belonging to the different Vedic-Schools When the sense is that of repetition, is singular.

The word चरण means a school or branch of any of the Vedas designated by the name of the person who founded such a branch and hence means such a person. The word अनुवाद means repetition by way of explanation, illustration or corroboration; that is to say, when a speaker demonstrates for some special purposes, a proposition which had already been demonstrated before, that is called anuvādā.

This aggregate is used with the aorist of the roots स्था and दृक् only; as उदगात् कठकालापम् 'kaṭha and kālāpa arose (again, further demonstrating their doctrines); प्रत्यगात् कठकीथुमम् 'kaṭha and kanthuma established again.

Why do we say 'when meaning repetition'? Observe उदगः कठकालापः or प्रत्यगः कठकीथुमः, when demonstration for the first time is meant. It is the aorist of स्था and दृक् which takes such a Dvandva and not any other verb or any other tense of these verbs; as:—अनन्दिपुः कठकालापः and उदगन्ति कठकालापः

Note:—This sūtra is translated thus by Mr. Iyangar, 'Aggregation alone is admissible between words denoting persons belonging to the different charāṇas of the Vedas, when they are used along with the aorist derived from the roots sthā and īṁ in the sense of recitation of the charāṇas as already learnt, as distinguished from learning them the first time.' Prof. Bohthlingk's translation is. 'The Dvandva Compound of the names of Vedic-Schools is singular, when such a school is repeatedly mentioned equally along with another.

BK. II. CH. IV. § 4-6.]

DVANDVA COMPOUND.

309

अध्वर्युक्रतुरनपुंसकम् ॥ ४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अध्वर्यु, क्रतुः, अ-नपुंस-
कम् । ( द्वन्द्व, एकवचनम् )

वृत्तिः ॥ अध्वर्यु क्रतुरनपुंसकम् ॥ ४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अध्वर्यु, क्रतुः, अ-नपुंस-
कम् । ( द्वन्द्व, एकवचनम् )

4. A Dvandva compound of words denoting
sacrifices (kratu) ordained by the Yajur (Adhvaryu) Veda, is
singular, provided they are never used in the neuter gender.

As, अकारवचेपम् 'the Arks and Aśvamedha sacrifices,' सायाह्नातिरामम्
'the Sāyāhna and Atirātra sacrifices.

Why do we say 'Yajur-veda' sacrifices? Observe रघुवृत्तौ 'the Ishu
and Vajra ceremonies,' उद्भिद्वलभिदौ ॥

Why do we say 'when not in the neuter gender'? Observe राजसूय-
वाजपेयौ 'the Rājasūya and Vājapeya sacrifices.'

Why have we दर्पणोर्धनाचौ? Because the word क्रतुः is a technical
term applying only to Soma-sacrifices and not any sacrifices in general.
Therefore, though Darśa and Paurṇamāsa are Yajur-veda ceremonies,
they not being Soma ceremonies, the present rule does not apply.

अध्ययनतोऽविषकृष्टारुयानाम् ॥ ५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अध्ययनतः, अवि
प्रकृष्ट-रुयानाम्, ( द्वन्द्व, एकवचनम् )

वृत्तिः ॥ अध्ययनेन निमित्तेन ये ऽनविषकृष्टा प्रत्यायन्ता आरुया तेषां द्वन्द्व एवमद्वपति ॥

5. A Dvandva compound of words denoting
(persons who have studied) subjects, which in their order of
study are not remote from each other, is singular.

As, पदकक्रमकम् 'a person who has studied the pada arrangement
and a person who has studied the krama arrangement; so also क्रमकवार्तिकम्.

Why do we say 'order of study'? Observe पितापुत्रौ 'father and son.'
Why do we say 'not remote'? See याचिकवैताकरणौ 'sacrifice-knower and
the grammarian.'

जातिरप्राशिनाम् ॥ ६ ॥ पदानि ॥ जातिः, अप्राशिनाम्,
( द्वन्द्व, एकव० ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ जातिराशिनां शब्दानां द्वन्द्व एकवद्वपति, प्राशिनो क्लेशित्वा ॥

6. A Dvandva compound of words signifying
jāti (genus) which are not names of living beings, is singular.

310

DVANDVA COMPOUND.

[BK. II. CH. IV. § 6, 7.

Thus आराधित 'the probe and the knife'; पानाच्छकुलि 'fried rice and barley cake.'

Why do we say 'words denoting genus'? Observe नन्दकपाञ्चनयी 'Nandaka and Panchajanya.'

Why do we say 'not of living'? See ब्रह्मचर्यत्रियो 'Brahmanas and the Kshatriyas.'

This rule applies to the jāti or genus names of substances (द्रव्यजाति) and not the jati names of qualities and actions. (युवकियाजाति), Thus दपरव-गन्धस्पर्शः 'colour, savour, odour, and tangibility'; गमनाकुट्टमभवारवाति 'going, contraction and expansion.'

Even with jati names of substances, the Dvandva compound takes singular, only when the objects are spoken of collectively as a class; when, however, the individuals belonging to a class are indicated, the proper number should be employed; as, इह कुण्डे बदरामलकानि तिष्ठन्ति 'in this bowl are the badari and amalaki fruits.'

The words जाति 'genus,' द्रव्य 'substance,' युग 'quality' and क्रिया 'action' are technical terms of Indian Logicians. Jāti has already been explained. Substances are nine: earth, water, light, air, ether, time, space, soul, and mind. Qualities are twenty-four: colour, savour, odour tangibility, number, dimension, severity, conjunction, disjunction, priority, posteriority, weight, fluidity, viscosity, sound, understanding, pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, effort, merit, demerit and faculty. There are five actions: throwing upwards, throwing downwards, contraction, expansion, and going.

विशिष्टलिङ्गो नदी देशोऽग्रामाः ॥ ७ ॥ पदानि ॥ विशिष्ट-लिङ्गः, नदी, देशः, अग्रामाः, (द्व०१०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ विशिष्टलिङ्गानां निम्नलिङ्गानां नदीयाचिनां शब्दानां देशयाचिनां च ग्रामवर्जितानां द्रव्यं पङ्कवद्वपति ॥

वास्तिकम् ॥ अग्रामा द्रव्यं नगराणां प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

वास्तिकम् ॥ उभयतद्व ग्रामाणां प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

7. A Dvandva compound of words of different genders, denoting names of rivers and countries, but not of towns, is singular.

Thus गंगायोकम् 'the Ganges and the Sona.' कुरवाः + कुरवेव = कुरकुरवेव 'the country of the Kurus and the Kurukshetra.' उदृश्यैरावती कुरकुर वाङ्मलम् ॥

Why do we say 'of different genders'? Observe गंगायवृते 'the Ganges and the Yamuna.' Both being feminine gender, so also भद्रकवाः ॥

BK. II. CH. IV. § 7-9.] DVANDVA COMPOUND.

311

Why do we say 'rivers and countries'? Observe कुकुटनदुवै 'the hen and the pea-hen.'

Why do we say 'not of a town'? See जाम्बवयालुकिन्ची 'Jāmbaba and Sālukini, which are the names of two villages or grama.

We have taken the word 'river,' as the word 'country' does not include 'river.' So also 'mountains' are not included; as कैलायगन्धमादने the Kailasa and the Gandhamadana.'

Vart:—The prohibition extends to villages and towns (grāma) but not to cities, (Nagara), as मथुरापाटलिपुलं 'the cities of Mathura and Patali-putra.'

Vart:—When a compound consists of two words, one a town and the other a city, the prohibition applies; as चोयंकेतवते 'the city of Saurya and the village of Ketavata.'

बुद्रजन्तवः ॥ ८ ॥ पदानि ॥ बुद्र-जन्तवः, (द्वन्द्व एकवचनम्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ बुद्रजन्तु बाचिनां द्वन्द्व एकवद्भवति ॥

8. A Dvandva compound of words signifying small animals, is singular.

Thus ब्रूकालिवम् 'the louse and the nil'; दंजनयकम् 'the bug and the mosquito.' The word बुद्रजन्तु means an animal of a very small size. Some say that animals not having bones are called बुद्रजन्तु, (invertebrates); others say, those which are small in size; others say, all below the mongoose are ksh udrajantu.

येयां च विरोधः शाश्वतिकः ॥ ९ ॥ पदानि ॥ येयां, च, विरोधः, शाश्वतिकः (द्वन्द्वः, एकव०) ॥

वृत्ति ॥ येयां शाश्वतिको विरोधस्तद्वाचिनां यमुदानां द्वन्द्व एकवद्भवति ॥

9. A Dvandva compound of words signifying those animals only among whom there is permanent enmity i. e., natural and eternal antipathy or quarrel, is singular.

The word विरोधः means enmity : and शाश्वतिकः means permanent.

Thus, मार्जारभूषकम् 'the cat and the rat'; खयुगालम् 'the dog and the jackal'; अचिनकुलम् 'the snake and the mongoose.'

Why do we say 'natural and eternal'? Observe गोपालिया लंकायनाः जलदायन्ते 'Gaupali and Salankayana are quarrelling.'

The force of the word च in the aphorism is that of एव 'only.' Dvandva compounds of such animals only are invariably singular; no other rule, even if otherwise applicable, would apply to such compounds.

312

DVANDVA COMPOUND.

[BK. II CH. IV. § 9-11.]

Thus rule 12 says that Dvandva compounds of beasts and birds, is optionally singular. That rule (by I. 4, 2.) would have set aside the present rule. But it prevents that, and no optional plural number is allowed in case of beasts or birds that are naturally at war; as अय्यनद्विषम्, 'the horse and the buffalo'; काकोलुकम् 'the crow and the owl.'

शूद्राणामनिरवसितानाम् ॥ १० ॥ पदानि ॥ शूद्राणाम्, अ-निरव-सितानाम्, (द्वन्द्वः, एकव०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अनिरवसितशूद्रवाशिनां गवदानां द्वन्द्व एकवद्भवति ॥

10. A Dvandva compound of words denoting those classes of Sādras who have not been expelled from the communion of higher classes, is singular.

Thus, तन्नावस्करम् 'the carpenter and the blacksmith'; रजकतन्तुवायम् 'the washerman and the weaver.'

The word अनिर्वासित means one not expelled (from the dish).

A Sādra who can take food from the dish of a higher class, without permanently defiling that vessel, is called an Anirvasita Sādra.

Why do we say 'not expelled'? Observe चण्डालभृतपाः 'the Chandala and the Mritapa.'

गवाश्वपुम्तीति ॥ ११ ॥ पदानि । गवाश्व-पुम्तीति, (एक-वचनम्, द्वन्द्वः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गवाश्वपुम्तीति कृतैकवद्भावानि द्वन्द्वरूपाणि साधुनि भवन्ति ॥

11. The word gavāśva, and others are also Dvandva compounds which take the singular number.

Thus गवाश्वम् 'the cow and the horse.' So also गवाविकम्.

गवाश्वादिः

1. गवाश्वम्. 2. गवाविकम्. 3. गवैडकम्. 4. अजाविकम्. 5. अजै-डकम्. 6. कुज्जवामनम्. 7. कुज्जकैरातकम्. 8. पुत्रपौत्रम्. 9. स्वचण्डालम्. 10. श्रीकुमारम्. 11. दासीमाणवकम्. 12. शाटीपिण्डकम्. 13. उद्गुरुम्. 14. उद्गुरुम्. 15. भुवनकृत्. 16. भुवपुरीपम्. 17. यकुन्तेवः. 18. भांयशोचितम्. 19. दर्भगवम्. 20. दर्भपुत्रीकम्. 21. अजुर्भगिरीपम्. 22. तुषोलपम्. 23. दासीदासम्. 24. कुटीकुटम्. 25. भगवतीभागवतम्.

*Vart*:—In this list, the forms as given, are singular; but when the same words assume different forms they may take either number. As गोस्वम् or गोस्वी. In this form of गो and अस्व the next 'rule' applies and option is allowed.

BK. II. Cu. IV. § 12, 13.]

DVANDVA COMPOUND

313

विभाषा वृक्षमृगतृणाधान्यव्यञ्जनपशुशकुन्यश्ववदवपूर्वापराधरोत्तराणाम् ॥ १२ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा, वृक्ष-मृग-तृण-धान्य-व्यञ्जन-पशु-शकुनि-अश्ववदव-पूर्व-अपर-अधर-उत्तराणाम्, (द्व०प०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वृक्ष मृग तृण धान्य व्यञ्जन पशु शकुनि अश्ववदव पूर्वापर अधरोत्तर हन्त्येतेषां दृष्ट्वा विभाषैकवदुभवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ वदुभवति ॥ फलसेना वनस्पतिमृगशकुनिवृत्तवन्तुधान्यतृणानाम् ॥

12. A Dvandva compound of words being the names of trees, wild animals, grass, corn, condiment, domestic beasts and birds, and the compounds aśva-vadava, purvā-para and adharottara, are optionally singular.

12. Thus, सृजन्यशोधम् or सृजन्यशोधाः 'the Plaksha and the Nyagrodha trees'; रूपप्रयत्नम् or रूपप्रयत्नाः 'the Ruru-deer and the spotted antelopes'; कुशकायम् or कुशकायाः 'the Kuśa grass and the Kāśa grass'; ब्रीडिववम् or ब्रीडिववाः 'the rice and the barley'; दधिपु व् or ते 'the curd and the butter'; गोमडिवव् or पाः 'the cow and the buffalo'; तित्तिरिकपिञ्जलम् or साः 'the Tittiri (a kind of partridge) and the Kapinjala birds'; अश्ववदवम् or वाः 'the horse and the mare'; पूर्वापरम् or रे 'the first and the last'; अधरोत्तरम् or रे 'the upper and lower.

Vart:—The Dvandva compound of words denoting names of fruits, army, large trees, wild animals, birds, small animals grain and grass, is singular, when a large number or quantity of these is spoken of; that is when a large number of them is taken collectively, the compound is singular, otherwise not; as, वदुरामलके तिष्ठतः 'a badari and an Āmalāki fruit are here'; रथिकाश्रारोही 'a charioteer and a horseman'; सृजन्यशोधौ 'a Plaksha and a Nyagrodha tree'; रूपप्रयत्नौ 'a Ruru and a Prishata deer'; इंसपकवाकी 'a Hansa and a Chakravaka bird'; कुशलिये 'a louse and nit'; ब्रीडिववी 'a brihi and yava grain'; कुशकायौ 'the kuśa and kāśa grass.

विपूतिषिद्धं चानधिकरणवाचि ॥ १३ ॥ पदानि ॥ विपूतिषिद्धं, च, अनधिकरण-वाचि, (विभाषा द्व० एक) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ विपूतिषिद्धार्थानां शब्दानामनधिकरणवाचिनामहव्यवाचिनां दृष्ट्वा एकवदुभवति विभाषातुकर्षणार्थं प्रकारः ॥

13. A Dvandva compound of words of contrary significations, but not being the names of concrete substances, is optionally singular.

Thus श्रीतोऽप्यक् or श्रीतोऽप्यक् 'cold and heat'; सुखदुःखं or सुखदुःखं 'pleasure and pain'; जोवितमरखं or जोवितमरखं 'life and death.'

The word विपूतिषिद्धं means words of contrary significations, च indicates the anuvritti of the word 'optionally' from the last sūtra.

314

DVANDVA COMPOUND.

[BK. II. CH. IV. § 13-16.

Why do we say 'of contrary significations'? Observe, कामकोशी 'lust and anger,' which are not of contrary significations.

Why do we say 'not being the names of substances'? Observe श्रीतोप्से उदके 'cold and warm waters,' which denote substances.

न दधिपय आदीनि ॥ १५ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, दधिपयः, आदीनि (द्व०१०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ दधिपय आदीनि शब्दरूपाणि नैकवद्भवन्ति ॥

14. The Dvandva compounds like 'dadhipaya' &c., are not singular.

Thus दधिपयसी 'the curd and the milk'; सर्पिर्भवुनी or मधुसर्पिणी 'the clarified butter and the honey.'

With this sūtra begins prohibition of singular number which previous sūtras would have caused.

The following is a list of such compounds:—

1. दधिपयसी. 2. सर्पिर्भवुनी or मधुसर्पिणी. 3. युग्मप्रजापती. 4. शिव-वैभवसी. 5. स्कन्दविभावसी. 6. परिबुद्धकीभिकी. 7. प्रबन्धीपसदी. 8. युग्म. कृष्णी. 9. इष्मारदिनी ॥ निपातनाद्वीपः ॥ 10. दीक्षातपसी. 11. ब्रह्मतपसी. 12. ने घातपसी. 13. अध्ययनतपसी. 14. उन्मूललवुचसे. 15. आद्यावसाने. 16. ब्रह्मनेषे. 17. ब्रह्मनेषे. 18. बाह्यमनेषे.

अधिकरणेतावत्वे च ॥ १५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अधिकरण-एता वत्वे, च, (न द्व०१०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अधिकरणं वर्णिपदार्थः, स हि समासस्यार्थस्याधारः तस्यैतावत्वे परिमाणे मध्यमाने द्वन्द्वो नैकवद्भवति ॥

15. A Dvandva compound denoting a fixed number (etavatva) of concrete things (adhikarna) is not singular.

As, दय इन्तोद्धाः 'ten sets of teeth and lips'; दयमार्द्रिकपाशविकाः 'ten sets of drum and panavika players.' Compare II. 4. 2.

विभाषा समीपे ॥ १६ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभाषा समीपे, (अधिकरणेता-वत्वे, द्वन्द्वः एकव०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अधिकरणेतावत्वस्य समीपे विभाषा द्वन्द्व एकवद्भवति ॥

16. A Dvandva compound, denoting an approximate number of concrete substances, is optionally singular.

BK. II. CH. IV. § 16-18]

SAMASAS.

315

As, उपदयं दन्तोः or उपदया दन्तोः 'nearly ten i.e., nine or eleven sets of teeth and lips; उपदयं नादिक्पापयिकम् or उपदया नादिक्पापयिकाः nearly ten (nine or eleven) mridanga and panava players.'

An indeclinable, when compounded with a numeral, may either be a Bahuvrihi or an Avyayibhava compound. When the compound is singular in form, it is Avyayibhava, and when it takes proper number-terminations, it is Bhuvrihi compound. As, उपदयं; उपदया (II. 2. 25).

स नपुंसकम् ॥ १७ ॥ पदानि ॥ स, नपुंसकम् (एकवचनम्, द्वन्द्वः, द्विगुः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ यद्यपयेकवद्भावो विदितः स नपुंसकलिङ्गो भवति द्विगुर्द्वन्द्वम् ॥
वात्तिकम् ॥ अकारान्तोः रपदो द्विगुः खिचां भाप्यते ॥
वात्तिकम् ॥ वाऽऽवन्तः खिचामिष्टः ॥
वात्तिकम् ॥ अनो नतोपञ्च वा च द्विगुः खिचाम् ॥
वात्तिकम् ॥ पात्रादिभ्यः प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

17. It, namely the Dvigu or the Dvandva compound, with regard to which singular number has been ordained by the above rules, is always a neuter gender.

As, दग्धवम् 'an aggregate of ten cows,' पाशिपादम् 'hands and feet,' गिरोग्रीवम् 'head and neck.'

This *sūtra* debars the operation of the rule by which a compound gets the gender of its subsequent member. See II. 4. 26.

*Vart*:—A Dvigu, the last member of which ends in short अ, is employed in the feminine gender only; as पञ्चवृत्ती, दशरथी.

*Vart*:—A Dvigu, the last member of which is a feminine word ending in आप् affix, is optionally feminine; as, पञ्चवृत्तम् or पञ्चवृत्ती.

*Vart*:—A Dvigu, the last member of which is a word ending in अम्, is optionally feminine and the न is elided; as पञ्चवृत्तम् or पञ्चवृत्ती.

*Vart*:—A Prohibition must be stated in the case of Dvigu compounds ending in पात्र &c., पञ्चपात्रम्; पञ्चवृत्तम्; त्रिपुत्रवृत्तम्.

अव्ययीभावश्च ॥ १८ ॥ पदानि ॥ अव्ययी भावः, च, (नपुंसकम्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अव्ययीभावश्च समासो नपुंसकलिङ्गो भवति ॥
वात्तिकम् ॥ पुत्रयुद्धिनाभ्यानः क्रीवतेभ्यते ॥
वात्तिकम् ॥ पयः संख्याव्ययादेः सकीवतेभ्यते ॥
वात्तिकम् ॥ क्रियाविधेयः ४ गं कर्मस्थं नपुंसकलिङ्गता च वक्तव्या ॥

316

SAMASAS.

[BK. II. CH. IV. § 18-20.

18. An Avyayibhāva (II. 1. 6.) compound is also neuter gender.

Thus, अचिन्ति 'pertaining to a woman; so also, उपकुमारी, उष्मसंगम &c.

But for this rule, an Avyayibhāva compound would have been either without any gender, if gender were to be regulated by its first member, which is generally an indeclinable, and which is the principal member in the compound; or it would have taken the gender of its subsequent member, like other compounds in which the last member is principal.

The force of च is to include cases not mentioned already.

Vart:—Neuter gender is employed after the word ऋत preceded by पुष्य or मुदिन; as पुष्याह्व 'sacred day'; मुदिनाह्व 'lucky day'.

Vart:—The word पय is neuter when compounded with a numeral or an Avyaya; as पुष्यय, पुष्यय, पुष्यय, पुष्यय.

Vart:—Adverbs, qualifying verbs, are put in the neuter gender and accusative case; as मुदु पयति 'he cooks mildly,' गोमन पयति 'he cooks well.'

तत्पुरुषोऽनञ् कर्मधारयः ॥ १९ ॥ पदानि ॥ तत्पुरुषः, अनञ् कर्मधारयः (नपुंसकम्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ नञ् कर्मधारय च बन्धित्वा नञ् कर्मधारय च नञ् कर्मधारय च बन्धित्वा नञ् कर्मधारय च बन्धित्वा नञ् कर्मधारय च बन्धित्वा नञ् कर्मधारय ॥

19. A Tat-purusha compound, with the exception of that which is formed by the particle nañ, and of the Karmadhārava compound, becomes neuter gender, in the cases explained in the following sūtras.

This is a governing sūtra, and regulates the sense of the succeeding aphorisms which show when a Tat-purusha may be neuter. Thus, बृहन्नवेनम् or. ना (II. 4. 25); but हृदयनो राजा (the compound not being Tat-purusha); अचैना (it being a compound with नञ्=अ); and परमचैना (it being Karmadhārava).

संज्ञायां कन्धोशीनरेषु ॥ २० ॥ पदानि ॥ संज्ञायाम्, कन्धा, उशीनरेषु, (तत्पुरुषः नपुंसकम्) ॥

वृत्ति ॥ संज्ञायां विषये कन्धा नञ् कर्मधारय च नञ् कर्मधारय च बन्धित्वा नञ् कर्मधारय च बन्धित्वा नञ् कर्मधारय च बन्धित्वा नञ् कर्मधारय ॥

20. When denoting an appellative, a Tatpurusha compound ending with the word kanthā 'town,' is neuter in gender, provided that it is the name of a town situated in the country of the Usinaras.

BK. II. CH. IV. § 20-22.]

SAMASAS.

317

As, शौचिकन्यम् 'the town of Saṃsāmi'; आङ्गुरकन्यम् 'the town of Ahwara.'

When not an appellative, the form is different; as, वीरकन्या. So also if the town is not in the country of the Uṣīnaras; as दासिकन्या.

This debars the rule (II. 4. 25.) by which a compound gets the gender of its subsequent term. (For accent see IV. 2. 124.)

उपज्ञोपक्रमं तदाद्याचिख्यासायाम् ॥ २१ ॥ पदानि ॥ उपज्ञा-उपक्रमं, तद्-आदि-आचिख्यासायाम् (तत्पुरुषः, नपुंसकम्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ उपज्ञोपक्रमं तदन्तस्तत्पुत्रयो नपुंसकलिङ्गो भवति तदाद्याचिख्यासायां तथा उपज्ञोपक्रमयोवाचिख्यासायां गन्ध मानायाम् ।

21. A Tat-purusha compound ending with the words 'upajñā' (invention) and 'upakrama' (commencement) is neuter in gender, when it is intended to express the starting point of a work which is first invented or commenced.

As, पाशिन्युपश्रमाकालापकं व्याकरणम् 'the grammars Kalāpa &c., had their commencement with Panini's invention'; व्याकरणं दुष्करणं 'Vyadi, invented Dushkaraṇa'; आङ्गुरकन्या प्रायाः 'the palace is an invention of rich folks'; नन्दोपक्रमाणि मानानि 'the measures are the invention of king Nanda.'

Of course, when it has not this sense, the neuter gender is not employed; as देवदशोपशो रथः 'the chariot made by Devadatta,' यददशोपक्रमो रथः 'the chariot commenced by Yajñadatta.' So also the sense may be that of invention &c., but when these words are not employed, the neuter gender is not used; as बाल्मीकिरलोकाः 'the slokas invented by Valmiki.' N. P. Prof. Bohtlingk gives पाशिन्युपश्रमकालकं व्याकरणम् 'The Grammar omitting the time of day is the work invented by Panini, (VI. 2. 14).

छाया बाहुल्ये ॥ २२ ॥ पदानि ॥ छाया, बाहुल्ये, (तत्पुरुषः, नपुंसकम्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ छायान्तस्तत्पुत्रयो नपुंसकलिङ्गो भवति बाहुल्ये गन्धमाने ॥

22. A Tat-purusha compound ending with the word chhāyā 'shadow' is neuter in gender when the sense is that of profuseness of the thing indicated by the first term.

Thus, यदनच्छावम् 'A crowd of locusts darkening the sky.' रुद्रछावम् 'the sugarcane shade i. e., groves of sugarcane.' Otherwise, कुण्डछाया 'the shadow of a wall.' (VI. 2. 14, accent.)

318

SAMASAS.

[BK. II. CH. IV. § 23-25.

The *sūtra* 25 gives optional neuter; this rule enjoins invariable neuter when chhaya has the sense of profuseness.

सभा राजामनुण्यपूर्वा ॥ २३ ॥ पदानि ॥ सभा, राजा-मनुण्य-
पूर्वा ( तत्पुरुंनपुंसक ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ सभास्तत्पुरुषो नपुंसकलिङ्गो भवति, या चेत् सभा राजपूर्वा मनुण्यपूर्वा च
भवति ॥

23. A Tatpurusha compound ending with the word *sabhā* 'court' is neuter, provided that it is preceded by (a word synonymous with) the word *Rājā*, or by a word denoting a non-human being.

As हनसमम् 'the King's Court.' हैरवरसमम् 'Lord's Court.'

But in राजसभा 'the King's Court,' the word is not neuter; for synonyms of राजा are only to be taken and not the word-form राजा; an apparent exception to Rule I. 1. 68.

So also रक्षसमम् 'the Court of the Rakshasas' पिशाचसमम् 'the Court of the Piśachas.'

But in काङ्क्षमा, दैवदत्तसभा &c., the word is not neuter; for the word non-human has a technical significance meaning Rakshasa or a monster.

अशाला च ॥ २४ ॥ पदानि ॥ अशाला, च, ( तत्पुरुं
नपुंसक ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अशाला च या सभा तदन्तस्तत्पुरुषो नपुंसकलिङ्गो भवति ॥

24. A Tat-purusha compound ending with the word *sabhā*, when it does not mean a house, but means concourse, is neuter.

As, श्रीसमम्, दासीसमम् 'the concourse of ladies and slaves;' otherwise अनायसमा 'the poor-house.'

विभाषा सेनासुराच्छायाशालानिशानाम् ॥ २५ ॥ पदानि ॥

विभाषा, सेना-सुर-छाया-शाला-निशानाम्, ( नपुंसकं, तत्पुरुषः ) ॥

वृत्ति ॥ सेना सुर-छाया शाला निशा इत्येवमस्तत्पुरुषो नपुंसकलिङ्गो भवति विभाषा ॥

25. A Tat-purusha compound ending with the words *senā* 'army' *surā* 'wine,' *chhāyā* 'shadow,' *śālā* 'house,' and *niśā* 'night,' is optionally neuter, with the exception of that which is formed by the particle *nañ* (II. 2. 6) and the *karmadhāraya* compound.

BK. II. CH. IV. § 25-21.]

As ब्राह्मणसेना, ब्राह्मणसेनम् 'the Brāhmana army,' यवसुरम्, यवसुरा 'the barley wine,' कुडयच्छायम्, कुडयच्छाया 'the shadow of the wall,' गोपालम्, गोपाला 'the cow house,' रमनिशम्, रमनिशा 'to-morrow night.' But अचैना 'non-army,' परमसेना good army,' the former being negative and the latter karmadharaya compound. For accent see VI. 2. 14. 123.

परवल्लिङ्गं द्रुद्रतत्पुरुषयोः ॥ २६ ॥ पदानि ॥ परवत्-लिङ्गम्, द्रुद्र-तत्पुरुषयोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ परस्य यल्लिङ्गं तद्भवति द्रुद्रस्य तत्पुरुषस्य च ॥

वाञ्छिकम् ॥ द्विगुप्तापन्नालं पूर्वमतिसमासेषु प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

26. The gender of Dvandva or Tat-purusha compound is like that of the last word in it.

This applies to Itaretara Dvandva or coupling by mutual conjunction कुक्कुटवद्गविनि 'those two (fem.) the cock and the peahen' नङ्गरीकुक्कुटविनि 'those two (mas.) the peahen and the cock.' The Samāhara Dvandva is always neuter. So also in Tat-purusha compound not especially mentioned in the previous aphorism: As अर्द्विपिप्पल्याः, अर्द्विपिप्पली 'half a pippali' अर्द्वकोशतकी.

Vart 1—Prohibition must be made in regard to (1) Dvigu compound, (2) compounds with मांस, आपन्न and, अलं, and (3) compounds with Gati words; as, पंचकपालः 'Purodasa prepared in five cups'; मांसजीविकः (मांस + जीविका) 'has obtained living,' आपन्नजीविकः, अलंजीविकः; निष्कौघान्धिः 'gone beyond Kauśambi.

पूर्ववदश्ववडवौ ॥ २७ ॥ पदानि ॥ पूर्ववद्, अश्व-वडवौ, (लिङ्गम्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अश्ववडयोः पूर्ववल्लिङ्गं भवति ॥

27. The gender of the compound of the word nāva 'horse' and vaḍava 'a mare,' is like that of the first word in it.

This applies where the compound is not an aggregate by rule II. 4. 12; in that case it will be neuter, अश्ववडवाविनि; अश्ववडवाम्, अश्ववडवैः &c., (in every number and case) 'those two (mas.) the horse and the mare.' This is an exception to the last and general rule, by which the gender of the subsequent term, guides the gender of the whole compound.

हेमन्तेशिशिरावहोरात्रे च छन्दसि ॥ २८ ॥ पदानि ॥ हेमन्ते-शिशिरी, अहो-रात्रे, च, छन्दसि, (पूर्ववत्, लिङ्गम्) ॥

SAMASAS.

[BK. II. CH. IV. § 28-30.]

देनन्तधिरानुद्वां भीषामि, अद्वारात्रे इदं ब्रूः ॥

This aphorism debars the general rule given in II. 4. 26.

This applies to these words in all cases and numbers, not being confined to them in the dual number, though exhibited in the sūtra in the dual number, as:—पूर्वपश्चात्त्वः, अपरपश्चात्त्वः, अद्वारात्रात्त्वः 'The white fortnight is fuel-wood, the black fortnight is the dung-cake, and days and nights are bricks (of the altar of sacrifice).'

रात्राह्नाहाः पुंसि ॥ २९ ॥ पदानि ॥ रात्र-अह्न-अहाः, पुंसि ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ अनुवाकादयः पुंसीति वक्तव्यम् ॥

29. The Dvandva and Tatpurusha compound ending with rātra and ahna and aha are spoken of in the masculine.

These words refer to kṛit and Samāsanta affixes. Thus the word रात्र is formed by रात्रि+अह्न (V. 4. 87) अह्न is formed by V. 4. 88 and अह्न by V. 4. 91. The general rule II. 4. 26 also does not apply here.

Vart:—The words अनुवाक &c., are masculine, as अनुवाकः, धनुवाकः, भूकवाकः &c.

अपथं नपुंसकम् ॥ ३० ॥ पदानि ॥ अपथम्, नपुंसकम् ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अपथ शब्दो नपुंसकलिङ्गो भवति ॥

30. The Tatpurusha word apatham 'a bad road' is neuter.

अपथनिदम् 'this (neuter) is a bad road' अपथानि गाइते भूह्नः 'the fool roams on wrong roads.' But अपथोदेशः a (masc.) 'a roadless country.' Here the compound being Bahuvrīhi the word is masculine so; also अपथा नगरी ॥

BK II. CH IV. § 31]

SAMASAN.

321

अर्धर्चाः पुंसी च ॥ ३१ ॥ पदानि ॥ अर्धर्चाः, पुंसी, च,
( नपुंसकम् ) ॥

पुंसीः ॥ अर्धर्चाः, पन्वा पुंसी नपुंसकम् च भाग्यन्ते ॥

31. The words 'ardharcha' &c., are spoken of in masculine and neuter.

As, अर्धर्चः and अर्धर्चः 'half a verse,' गान्धः and गान्धः 'cow-dung.' These twofold genders sometime, convey different meanings, the masculine form having one meaning and the neuter, another. Thus पन्द्रः 'treasure,' पन्द्रः or पन्द्रः 'lotus,' पन्द्रः 'treasure,' and पन्द्रः or पन्द्रः 'conch-shell,' पन्द्रः or पन्द्रः 'ghost.' But when it is a verbal noun, it takes the gender of the word it qualifies. वैष्णवः or वैष्णवः 'salt'; but when it is considered as a derivative word meaning 'born in or belonging to the sea' it takes the gender of the word it qualifies. सारः 'best' सारः 'compendium.' So पनः and पनः.

इदनोऽन्वादेशेऽश्नुदात्त तृतीयादी ॥ ३२ ॥ पदानि ॥ इदनः, अन्वादेशे, अश, अनुदात्तः तृतीयादी ॥

मुक्तिः ॥ इदनोऽन्वादेशे विश्वस्य देशो भवत्युदत्तमुतृतीयादी विभक्तौ परतः ॥

32. In the room of idam 'this,' in case of its re-employment in a subsequent member of the same sentence and referring to the same thing (anvādeśa) there is the substitution of as which is anudātta *i. e.*, gravely accented, when the third case-affix and the rest follow.

The word अन्वादेश means literally saying (ādesa) 'after' (anu) or after-say or re-employment.

अश् (actually अ) replaces इदन् [in] all cases except the nominative and the accusative, when anvādeśa or repetition is implied. अश् replaces the whole of इदन् by 55 and not only the final अ. Anvādeśa means repeating in a second sentence with reference to the preceding in which it has already been used. Both pronouns, the antecedent and the subsequent, must refer to the same object. As, आभ्याम् आभ्याम् रात्रिधीता, अये आभ्यामहस्यधीतम् 'These students studied in the night and they have read in the day also.' The substitute अश् will replace इदन्, even when the latter takes the affix अकश् (V. 3. 7. 1.)

BK. II. CH. IV. § 32-34.]

SAMASAS.

323

अस्मि खाद्याय कण्वलं देहि, अयो अस्मि खाद्याय देहि ' Give this student a blanket and give him also a cloth'. अस्मि खाद्याय होयत भीतय, अयो अस्मि खाद्याय, ' this student's conduct is excellent, and his wealth is great.'

So also when the affix अस्मि (V. 3. 71) comes after the Pronominal as इस्माभ्यां खाद्याय रात्रिधीता, अयो अस्मि खाद्याय।

The mere mentioning in a subsequent sentences is not anvāḍeśa : it is the employment again of what has been employed to direct one operation, to direct another operation. Therefore the rule does not apply here :—देवदत्तं भोजय, इमं यदवत्तम् ' feed Devadatta and this Yajñadatta.'

एतदस्ततसीस्ततसी चानुदात्ती ॥ ३३ ॥ पदानि ॥ एतदः, अ-तसीः
अ-तसी, च, अनुदात्ती, (अन्वादे, अम्, अनुदात्तः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ एतदेऽन्वेदेविवयस्य अन्वादे भवति अनुदात्ततसीः परतः ॥ ती चापि
अतसावनुदात्ती भवतः ॥

33. In the room of एतद् in case of its re-employment there is the substitution of the gravely accented अस्मि when the affixes अ (V. 3. 10) and तद् (V. 3. 7) follow, and the affixes अ and तद् are anudatta also (gravely accented.)

Thus अस्मि 'here,' and अस्मि 'hence' in the following :—एतस्मिन् प्राणे
कुलं वसन्तः; अयो अस्मि कुला अभिमते । ' We live in this (etasmin) village, happily, therefore let us read with full devotion in this (atra).' एतस्मिन्नान्नात्मनो
अभिमत, अयो अस्मि खाद्यायप्यभिमत । ' Learn from this student Prosody and also learn from him Grammar.' By rule V. 3. 5. अस्मि is declared to be the substitute of एतद्; its repetition here is to indicate that this अस्मि of anvāḍeśa is anudatta.

द्वितीयाटीः स्वेनः ॥ ३४ ॥ पदानि ॥ द्वितीया-टा-ओस्सु, एनः,
( इदम्, एतद्, अन्वादे, अनुदात्ते )

वृत्तिः ॥ द्वितीया टा ओम् इत्येतेषु परत इदनेतदोरन्वादेराविवयवोरेनशब्दवादे भवति
अनुदात्तः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ एतद्विति मयुं यतैकवचने वक्तव्यम् ॥

34. When an affix of the 2nd case or टा (Ins. Sing.) or ओम् (Loc. dual) follows, अ which is anudatta is the substitute of एतद् and एतद् in the case of its re-employment.

324

ARDHADHATUKA SUBSTITUTES.

[Bk. II. Ch. IV. § 34-35.]

The word **दत्त** is also understood in this *sūtra* though it was not so in the last. This skipping is technically called 'frog-leap.' Thus:—
**दत्त** or **पत्ते** **दत्ते** **दत्ते** **दत्ते** **दत्ते** **दत्ते** 'teach this pupil Prosody, and teach him Grammar also,' **अने** or **पते** **दाते** **दाते** **दाते** **दाते** 'this pupil studied in the night and he studied in the day also,' **अनयो** or **पतयो** **दातयो** **दातयो** **दातयो** **दातयो** 'the family of these two students is respectable and their wealth is great.'

*Vart*:—The word **पत्ते** neuter and singular, is also used in *anvādeśa*: as, **दत्ते** **दत्ते** **दत्ते** **दत्ते** 'bring this bowl and wash it.' The above three *Sūtra* regulate the accent only of certain pronouns.

**आहू-धातुके ॥ ३५ ॥ पदानि ॥ आहू-धातुके ॥**

**दूति ॥ पदनि ॥ यहू-धातुके ॥**

35. The clause 'when the affix is *Ardhadhātuka*' is understood in the following aphorisms up to aphorism 58 of this chapter.

Thus it will be taught in *sūtra* 42, 'that **दत्ते** is the substitute of **दत्ते** when **दत्ते** follows.' The words 'when the affix is *Ardhadhātuka*' must be read into the *sūtra* to complete the sense. The result will be that in the *Ardhadhātuka* **दत्ते** namely the **आशीर्वाद** or the Benedictive mood, **दत्ते** is replaced by **दत्ते**, but not so in the *Sārvadhātuka* **दत्ते** *i. e.*, the Potential mood (विधिविद्). Thus, Benedictive **दत्ते** 'may he kill'; but Potential **दत्ते** let him kill.'

The word **आश्वानुके** is in the 7th case; the force of this case-affix here is not that given in I. 1. 66. *i. e.*, the *sūtra* does not mean 'when an *Ardhadhātuka* affix follows.' But the 7th case has the force of indicating the subject, the meaning of the *sūtra* being 'when the subject is an *Ardhadhātuka* affix.' The result of this explanation is, that the various substitutions enjoined hereafter should be made first, and then the respective affixes should be applied. Thus whenever we want to affix any *Ardhadhātuka*-affix to **अत्ते** 'to be,' we must first substitute **दत्ते** for it, and then take the proper *Ardhadhātuka*-affix which would come with regard to **दत्ते**. Thus we can apply **दत्ते** to **दत्ते** by rule III. 1. 97 which says: 'after verbs ending in vowels **दत्ते** is applied.' But this affix could never have been applied to **अत्ते** which ends in a consonant. Thus we have **अत्ते** to **दत्ते**. So the substitution does not depend upon any particular affix, but *Ardhadhātuka*-affixes as a class.

BK. II. Ch. IV § 36-37.]

ARDHADHATUKA SUBSTITUTES.

325

अदो जन्धिर्यसि किति ॥ ३६ ॥ पदानि ॥ अदः, जन्धिः, रूप्-
ति, किति, ( आर्दु-धातुके ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अदो जन्धिर्यस्सो भवति रूपि परतः तकारादौ च किति मतय्ये ॥

36. The word जन्धि is the substitute of अद् 'to eat,' when the affix रूप् (VII. 1. 37) or an *ardhadhātuka* किद affix beginning with त follows.

मजग्ग 'Having eaten.' ( म + अद् + रूप् = म + जन्ध् + म ). So also जन्ध 'eaten' ( अद् + क = जन्ध् + क ).

The क in जन्धि is merely for the sake of articulation and is not an *anubandha*, otherwise there would have been the insertion of the *nasal* न ( अद् ). So also the क in जन्धि &c., is merely for the sake of articulation. But अद् + क = जन्धः 'food' is an irregularity.

The employment of रूप् in this *sūtra* indicates the existence of this *Paribhāṣā*. 'A *bahirāṅga* substitution of रूप् supersedes even *antaraṅga* rules.' Because in case this maxim did not exist, the substitution of जन्ध् for अद् before रूप् which is taught in this *sūtra*, would follow already from the word किति (before that which is distinguished by an *indicatory* क) in this rule, i. e., जन्ध् would (by maxim 'that which is *bahirāṅga* is regarded as not having taken effect, or as not existing, when that which is *antaraṅga* has taken effect') first be substituted for अद् before क and रूप् afterwards for क.

Why do we say 'before affixes beginning with त'? Observe अदते 'is eaten.'

Why do we say 'before affixes having *indicatory* क'? Observe अजग्ग.

लुह्सनोपरस्तु ॥ ३७ ॥ पदानि ॥ लुह्सनोः, पस्तु ( अदः, आर्दुधा० ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लुह्सनि च परतोऽदो पस्तु आदेसो भवति ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ पस्तु भावेऽप्युपसंख्यानम् ॥

37. When *luñ* (aorist) or *san* (desiderative) follows पस्तु is the substitute of अद् 'to eat.'

अपसत्, अपसताम्, अपसत् 'he ate.' The लुह् in पस्तु is servile and indicates the substitution of अद् for क्ति of the *Aorist* (III. 1. 55.) So also in desiderative, as, जिपत्सति, जिपत्सतः जिपत्सन्ति 'wishes to eat.'

*Vart* :—The verb अद् is replaced by पत् when the affix अद् follows Thus म + अद् + अद् = पत् + अद् = मपतः 'voracious.'

826

ARDHADHATUKA-SUBSTITUTES.

[BK. II. CH. IV. § 38-40.

बजपोश्च ॥ ३८ ॥ पदानि ॥ षड्-अपोः, च, (अदः, षड्, आ०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ बनि बनि च परतोऽदो षड् आद्यो भवति ॥

38. And when the affix षड् and अप् follow षड् is the substitute of अद्.

पाशः 'food, grass,' अद्+षड्=पाश+अ (III. 3. 19). मयतः 'voracity.' १. म+अद्+अप्=म+पश.

बबुलं बन्धसि ॥ ३९ ॥ पदानि ॥ बबुलं, बन्धसि, (अदः, षड्, आ०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ बन्धसि बिनये बबुलमदो षड् आद्यो भवति ॥

39. In the chhandas (Vedas), षड् is diversely substituted for अद्.

षड्। बन्धसि बिनये बबुलमदो षड् आद्यो भवति ॥

The word बबुल is used in this sūtra and the word अन्यतरस्याम् in the next. There is evidently difference between the senses of these words; otherwise Pāṇini would not have employed them in such juxtaposition, had they been synonymous. For then the anuvritti of बबुल in the next sūtra would have been sufficient. The following verse indicates that difference.

कृषिद् मयुत्तिः कृषिदमयुत्तिः, कृषिदमिनापा कृषिदमदेव ।

बिनैर्विमानं बबुधा समीक्ष्य, बानुर्विमं बानुलकं बन्धसि ॥

'Sometimes they are, where there is no express rule for their application; sometimes they are not applied, in spite of an express rule for their application; sometimes they are optionally employed or not, and sometimes there is some other result, licence permitted by the rule.' Thus in षड् there is not elision of the penultimate.

लिट्यन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ लिटि, अन्यतरस्याम्, (अदः, षड्, आः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लिटि परतोऽदोऽन्यतरस्यां षड्। बिनैर्विमं भवति ॥

40. When लिट् (Perfect) follows षड् is optionally the substitute of अद्.

सपाव or आद 'he ate,' सबदुः or आददुः 'they two ate,' सदुः or आदुः 'they all ate.' The word सबदुः is thus formed:—षड्+अदुः=षड्+षड्+अदुः

BK. II. CH. IV. § 40-42.]

ARDHADHATUKA-SUBSTITUTES.

327

(VI. 1. 8) = च + च + च + च (VII. 4. 60) = च + च + च (VII. 4. 62)
= च + च + च (VIII. 4. 58) = च + च + च (VI. 4. 98.) = च (VIII.
3. 60).

वेजो वधिः ॥ ४९ ॥ पदानि ॥ वेजः, वधि, ( लिल्यन्यतरस्याम्,
आह्वः ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वेजो वधिरादेशो भवति अन्यतरस्यां लिङ्गि परतः ॥

41. When लिङ् follows, वधि is optionally the substitute of ' वेत्तु to weave.'

In the Perfect tense thus we have two roots: Let us first take
वेत्तु. Then we have regularly वे + लिङ् = वे + चत् = वधो. The roots in
व, वे and वो are treated like roots ending in वा thus:—

[tbl-0.md](tbl-0.md)

When however we take the base वध्, the व being for the sake
of articulation only, we have the following forms:— वध् + चत् = वध् + वध्
+ अ (VI. 1. 8) = वध् + वध् + अ (VI. 1. 17) = वधाय; the व is not changed into
व by VI. 1. 38. In this dual we have वध् + चत् = वध् + चत् (VI. 1. 15)
= व + वध् + चत् (VII. 4. 60) = वधयुः The affix चत् being किंतु affix by
rule I. 2. 5 there is samprasāraṇa before reduplication. Thus we have
वधाय, वधयुः, वधयुः. Further by rule VI. 1. 39 before किंतु affixes व may be
optionally substituted for व, i. e., वधयुः or वधयुः and वधयुः or वधयुः

इतो वध लिङ्गि ॥ ४२ ॥ पदानि ॥ इनः, वध, लिङ्गि ( आह्वं
धातुके ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इन्तेभीतोभेदहस्ययनादेशो भवति लिङ्गि परत आह्वंधातुके ॥

42. वध is the substitute of वध 'to kill' when the
Ardhadhātuka लिङ्ग (Benedictive) follows.

वधात्' my he kill,' वधास्ताम्' may they two kill,' वधायुः,' may they
all kill.'

The substitute वध, ends with short अ this अ is elided. This elision
being like the original (sthānivat I. 1.-56), in forming the Aorist, वध्, we
have वध + ० + वध = वधवीत्. Here zero being sthānivat prevents
the vriddhi of अ of व which otherwise would have take place by VII. 2. 7.

328

ARHADHATUKA-SUBSTITUTES.

[BK. II. CH. IV. § 43-45.

लुडि च ॥ ४३ ॥ पदानि ॥ लुडि, च (हनो, बध, आ०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ लुडि च परतो हनो वध इत्ययमादेयो भवति ॥

43. And when छह (Aorist) follows, वध is the substitute of छह.

अवधीत् 'he killed,' अवधीहान् 'they two killed.' The division of this aphorism from the last sūtra (yoga-vibhāga) indicates that the next rule applies to Aorist only and not to Benedictive as well. There is no option in Benedictive Atmanepada.

आत्मनेपदेऽन्यतरस्याम् ॥ ४४ ॥ पदानि ॥ आत्मनेपदेषु, अन्य-तरस्याम्, (हनो, बध, लुडि, आः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पूर्वेण नित्ये माते विकल्पं वध्यते । आत्मनेपदेषु परतो हनो लुड्यन्यतरस्यां वध इत्ययमादेयो भवति ॥

44. When Atmanepada affixes follow, वध is optionally the substitute of छह in the लुह (Aorist).

Thus आवधित् or आहत; आवधितानाम् or आहतानाम्; आवधित् or आहत.

The verb छह becomes Atmanepadi when preceded by आ (I. 3. 28) By sūtra I. 1.14, the Aorist-affixes in the Atmanepada are कित् after छह and by VI. 4. 37 the न is elided before कित् affixes then by VIII. 2. 27 the च is elided. Thus आहत + चित् + त = आहत.

इयो गा लुडि ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ इयः, गा, लुडि, (आ०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ इयो गा इत्ययमादेयो भवति लुडि परतः ॥

वार्तिकम् ॥ इरावधिक इति वक्तव्यम् ॥

45. गा is the substitute of the root छह when लुह follows.

अगात् 'he went' (II. 4. 77) अगाताम् 'they two went' अनु: 'they all went.' The repetition of the word लुह in this sūtra though is anuvṛiti was coming from the last aphorisms, indicates that there is no option allowed even in the Atmanepada, गा being the invariable substitute in all the Padas. Thus अगाधि भवता you, went.' The form अगात् is thus evolved अ+गा+चित्+त=, अगात् (II. 4. 77.)

Vart:—गा is the substitute of छह 'to remember' in the Aorist as it is of छह. Thus अभ्यगात् 'he remembered.' अभ्यगाताम्, अभ्यग्. The root छह belongs to Adādi class.

BK. II. CH. IV. § 46-49.]

ARDHADHATUKA-SUASTITUTION.

329

श्री गनिरबोधने ॥ ४५ ॥ पदानि ॥ श्री, गनि:, अबोधने,
( इष: ) ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ श्री परत इकोऽबोधनार्थस्य गनिरादेयो भवति ॥

46. When the affix चि (Causal) follows, गनि is the substitute of इक् when the sense is not that of 'informing' but that of 'going'.

गनयति 'makes him go' गनयत:, गनयन्ति &c. But मस्याययति 'causes to believe.' अभिगनयति. The इ of गनि is for articulation. So also इक् to 'remember'; as, अभिगनयति ॥

सनि च ॥ ४० ॥ पदानि ॥ सनि, च, ( इष:, अबोधने,
गनि: ) ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ सनि परत इकोऽबोधनार्थस्य गनिरादेयो भवति ॥

47. And when च (Desiderative) follows, गनि is the substitute of च् when the sense is not that of 'informing.'

जिगनियति 'wishes to go' जिगनियत:, जिगनियन्ति. But अर्थात् मतीनियति 'he wishes to inform the meaning.' So also with इक्, as अभिजिगनियति. The yogavibhāga indicates that the anuvritti of च् only runs in the next sūtra and not of चि. The form is thus evolved in the Parasmaipada; चन्+गच् = गच् + गच् + च (VI. 1. 9) = ग + गच् + च (VII. 4. 60) = च + गच् + च (VII. 4. 62) = च + गच् + इट् + च (VII. 2. 50) = जिगनिय, and then we add the personal terminations.

इकश्च ॥ ४८ ॥ पदानि ॥ इक:, च, ( सनि, गनि: ) ॥

वृत्ति: ॥ इकश्च सनि परतो गनिरादेयो भवति ॥

48. And of इक् 'to study,' गनि is the substitute when च् follows.

अभिजिगनियते, ० चते, ० चन्ते 'he wishes to study.' The root इक् is always preceded by the preposition अभि. This will be Atmanepadi by I. 3. 12 and I. 1. 56. The form is similarly evolved by the application of rules VII. 2. 58. and VI. 4. 16.

गाङ् लिटि ॥ ४९ ॥ पदानि ॥ गाङ्, लिटि, ( इक: ) ॥

यन्ति: ॥ गाङ्ग्रादेयो भवतीको लिटि परतः ॥

ARDHADHATUKA SUBSTITUTION.

[BK. II. CH. IV. § 49, 51.

49. गाह् is the substitute of ण् when लिद् (Perfect) follows.

The substitute being like its original (I. 1. 68.) गाह् would have been Atmanepadi, even without the indicatory, ण्. Why has then this ण् been added to it? The object is that in the sūtra 1. 2. 1. गाह् there should mean this substitute गाह् and not the verb गाह् 'to go.'

Thus we get अविश्वने 'he studied'. अविश्वने, अविश्वने. See VI. 4. 64 and III. 4. 8.

विभावा लुङ्खकोः ॥ ५७ ॥ पदानि ॥ विभावा, लुङ्खकोः ( ण्कः, वि, गाह् ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ण्कि ण्कि च परत ण्को विभावा गाङ्देवो भवति ॥

50. गाह् is optionally the substitute of ण् when ण् (Aorist) and ण् (Conditional Future) follow.

Let us take the case when गाह् replaces ण्. The affixes of ण् and ण् are treated as ण् by 1. 2. 1. and then by the Rule VI. 4. 66 (When an ardhadhatuka affix, beginning with a consonant and distinguished by an indicatory ण or ण् follows; then let ण् be the substitute of long ण of the verbs termed ण् and of ण्, ण्, ण्, ण्, ण्, ण्), we get अव्यगीत् (अवि + अ + गी + ण्), अव्यगीतात्, अव्यगीत्. In the alternative we have अव्यै, अव्यैतात् and अव्यैत.

So also in ण्; as अव्यगीत्, अव्यगीत्, अव्यगीत्, or in the alternative, अव्यैत्, अव्यैत् and अव्यैत्.

गौ च संख्यको, ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ गौ, च, सन्-यको, ( ण्कः, गाह्, विभावा ) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गौ ण्परे ण् परे च परत ण्को विभावा गाङ्देवो भवति ॥

51. गाह् is optionally the substitute of ण् in the causative वि, when that causative takes the affix san (desiderative) and chan (Aorist.)

अविनियाविवि or अव्याविविवि 'he desires to teach.' The form is thus evolved : ण् + ण् = ण् (VII. 3. 36); then by the rules already stated, we get the above form with the affix ण्. अव्यगीत् or अव्याविवि 'he taught.' The ण् is changed into ण् by VI. 1. 48. Thus ण् + ण् = ण् + ण् = ण् + ण् + ण् = ण्. This rule applies to the desideratives of causatives and aorist of causatives.

By. II. Ch. IV. § 52-54.]

ARDHADHATUKA SUBSTITUTIONS.

331

अस्तेभू ॥ ५२ ॥ पदानि ॥ अस्तेः, भूः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अस्तेभूतेर्भू इत्यवगादेशो भवति आर्द्धपादुके ॥

52. भू is the substitute of the verb अस् 'to be,' when an *ardhadhātuka* affix is to be applied.

भविता 'he will be,' भवितुम् 'in order to be,' भवितव्यम् 'must be.' Now the Perfect tense affixes are also *ardhadhātuka* affixes (III. 4. 115). The Perfect of अस् is therefore the same as that of भू, namely, वसुव &c. There is, however, an important exception to this rule, namely, when अस् is employed as an auxiliary verb in forming Periphrastic Perfect of other verbs. In that case अस् forms its Perfect tense regularly, आस आसवुः आसुः &c. This apparent breach of the present *sūtra* is explained by taking the term कुसु in III. 1. 40 as a *Pratyāhāra* including कू, भू and अस्, and if अस् could not form its Perfect in the regular way, its inclusion in this *Pratyāhāra* would be useless; hence we conclude, that as an auxiliary verb, अस् forms its Perfect regularly.

ब्रुवो वचिः ॥ ५३ ॥ पदानि ॥ ब्रुवः, वचिः, (आ०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ब्रुवो वचिरादेशो भवति आर्द्धपादुके बिषये ॥

53. वचि is the substitute of बू 'to speak' when any *ardhadhātuka* affix is to be applied.

वक्ता 'he will speak,' वसुव 'in order to speak.' The बू of वचि is for the sake of articulation only. The substitute being like the principal, वसु is *Atmanepadi* when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, as कचे 'he spoke,' वसुदे 'he will speak.'

वसिहः रूपान् ॥ ५४ ॥ पदानि ॥ वसिहः, रूपान्, (आ०) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ वसिहः रूपानदेशो भवति आर्द्धपादुके ॥

वासिकम् ॥ खगादिरव्ययमादेश इषुदे ॥

वासिकम् ॥ वनेने प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

वासिकम् ॥ असनयोइ प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ॥

वासिकम् ॥ वसुलं संधाब्रह्मोरिति वक्तव्यम् ॥

54. रूपान् is the substitute of वसिह् 'to perceive, to tell,' when any *ardhadhātuka* affix is to be applied.

आस्थाता 'he will perceive or tell'; अस्वातुम् 'in order to tell'; अस्वातव्यम् 'must be told.' The substitute being like the principal, वसिह् being always *Atmanepadi* (I. 3. 12), रूपान् would have also been always *Atmanepadi*. But in that case the letter भू would have no scope; it therefore follows that रूपान् is not always *Atmanepadi*, but under conditions mentioned in I. 3. 72.

Vart:—This substitute is also said to begin with कृण instead of रुच. Thus आकृणाता, आकृणातु, आकृणातव्यं.

Vart:—Prohibition must be stated when meaning 'exclusion'; as दुर्लभा: संचय्या: bad men should be excluded.'

Vart:—Prohibition must be stated when the affixes अच and अन follow: as नृपया राचय: the Rākshasas are cruel.' This is Vedic Sanskrit; modern नृपया. The meaning of the root चच् here, is 'to injure.' So also विचचय: पश्चित: here the affix is अन.

Vart:—Substitutes are made diversely in denoting appellatives and not qualities and in the Vedic Sanskrit; as अनच् 'food' (here the substitute अनच does not replace अच); वचकच् 'killer' (वच being substituted for हच् before पचुत); नाच 'body' (ना is substituted for हच् before the unādi affix हच्); विचचय: (here चच is not replaced by रुचा before अन); अजिरच् 'a court yard' (here अज is not replaced by डचे as the next sutra 56 requires.)

वृत्तिः ॥ लिटि परतश्चितः रुचाञ्देशो वा भवति ॥

55. रुचाञ् is optionally the substitute of चचिन् when लिट् (Perfect) follows.

The लिट् also is an ārdhadhātuka affix and by the last sātra रुचा, would always have been the substitute of चच्; the present sūtra makes this substitution optional, as आचरुचि, आचरुचुतु: and आचरुतु. In the alterative we have आचचचे, आचचचाते and आचचचिरे 'he told &c.

ELISION OF YUVAN AFFIX.

333

Vart:—Prohibition must also be stated (along with घञ् and अञ्) of the affix खप, as ससज्या 'a meeting, fame.'

Vart:—The substitution is optional before Ardhaḍhātukas beginning with a letter of वल् Pratyāhāra (all consonant except य) as मवैता or माजिता मवैतुव् or माजितुव्. See VI. 2. 144 for accent.

57. वी is optionally the substitute of अञ्, when the affix यु (III. 3. 15 &c.) follows.

This declares an option in case of the affix खप, the word यु in the Sūtra referring to this affix; as, मवयजः or माजनो दवहः 'driving stick or whip.'

ययक्षत्रियार्थजितो यूनि लुगशिजो ॥ ५८ ॥ पदानि ॥ यय-क्षत्रिय-आर्ष-जितः, यूनि, लुग्, अञ्-इजोः ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ ययान्तात् क्षत्रियगोत्रात् आर्षादजितव् पश्योरशिजोऽहूनि लुग् भवति ॥

यार्त्तिकव् ॥ अञ्-इजोः ॥

58. After a word ending with the Gotra affix ख (IV. 1. 151) and after a Gotra word denoting the descendant of a Kshatriya or a Rishi (seer), and after a word a word ending with a Gotra affix having an indicatory ञ्, the affix अञ् and इञ् employed in forming युवन् (IV. 1. 163) descendants, are elided by the substitution of खुक् ॥

1. Thus by sūtra IV. 1. 151 (the affix ख comes after कुव् &c., in denoting descendent) we get कुव् + ख = कौख्यः (VII. 2. 117) 'a grandson of Kuru.' This is a Gotra word (IV. 1. 162). Now in forming a word denoting a lower descendent than grandson, we add a Yuvan affix. Thus कौख्य + इञ् (IV. 1. 95). Now this इञ् is elided by the present sūtra, and we get the form कौख्यः which thus means both a Gotra and a Yuvan (IV. 1. 163) descendent of Kuru. So that कौख्यः is the name both of the father and the son.

Now it may be objected: 'the word कौख्यः belongs to the तिकादि class and by IV. 1. 154, it will take the affix किञ्. Do we, what we may, the form will be कौख्यावशिः (VII. 1. 2.) To this we reply, the word कौख्यः which we see in that list of तिक् &c., is not the word कौख्यः which we formed by adding ख under rule IV. 1. 151; that Tikādi word is formed by adding ख under rule IV. 1. 172, and is confined to Kshatriya. The कौख्यः which we have taken, denotes a Brahmin Gotra formed by IV. 1. 151.

334

ELISION OF YUVAN AFFIX.

[BK. II. CH. IV. § 58.

2. Now to give an example of a word denoting the descendent of a Kshatriya. We take IV. 1. 114. which tells us that 'the affix अणु may be added to the words which are the names of Rishis, or of persons belonging to the family of Andhaka, or Vrishinis or Kuru.' The Andhaka family, is a Kshatriya family, and खफरकः is a person of that family. Then खफरक + अणु = खफरकः 'a descendent of Svaphalka' This is a Gotra descendent. In forming Yuvan descendent we have खफरक + इणु. Now this इणु must be elided by the present sūtra. So that खफरकः means both father and the son.

3. Now to give an example of Rishis family. The sūtra last mentioned IV. 1. 114. will also hold here. We take the word वसिष्ठः; and वसिष्ठ + अणु = वसिष्ठः; the Yuvan affix इणु will similarly be elided after his; and thus the word वसिष्ठः means both the father and the son.

4. Then to take the example of Gotra word formed by affixes having indicatory ञ्. Thus sūtra IV. 1. 104. declares 'the affix अणु comes after the words विद् &c., in denoting Gotra descendents.' Thus विद् + अणु = वैदः; Then add इणु to denote Yuvan descent, and we have वैदः + इणु. By the present rule this इणु is elided and thus we have वैदः both for the father and the son.

The above examples show the elision of the affix इणु. Now we shall give example of the elision of the affix अणु. Now rule IV. 1. 154 says 'the affix किणु comes after the words तिक् &c., in denoting descendent.' Thus तिक् + किणु = वैकायनिः (VII. 1. 2.) Then to form the Yuvan descendent we add अणु by IV. 1. 83. Thus वैकायनि + अणु. By the present sūtra, this अणु is elided, and we have वैकायनिः both applicable to the father and the son. Other examples can be multiplied.

Why do we say 'there is elision only after these words'? The Yuvan affix will not be elided after other words. Thus rule IV. 1. 112 says:—'The affix अणु comes after विद् &c., in forming Gotra.' कौइड + अणु = कौइड. Now this is neither a word formed by वय nor is it the name of a Kshatriya or a Rishi; nor any affix having ञ् goes to form it. Therefore the Yuvan affix इणु will not be elided after this. Thus कौइड + इणु (IV. 1. 95) कौइडिः 'son of Kauhada.'

Why do we say 'affix denoting Yuvan descendent is elided? An affix not denoting a Yuvan descendent will not be elided. Thus the pupils of वामरव्य are called वामरव्याः which word is thus formed: वामरव्य + वय = वामरव्यः 'a descendent of Vāmaratha' (IV. 1. 115). Then to denote pupils we add अणु by IV. 2. 111. Thus वामरव्य + अणु = वामरव्यः 'a pupil of Vāmarathya.'

Why do we say 'Yuvan affix अणु and इणु are elided'? The other Yuvan affixes under similar circumstances are not elided. Thus the Yuvan

BK. II. CH. IV. § 57, 60.] ELISION OF YUVAN AFFIX.

335

descendent of दाचि (grandson of दव) will be दायायचः Here the affix फक् (IV. 1. 101) is not elided.

Vart:—All Yuvan affixes are elided after Gotra words not denoting Brahmin Gotras; as बौचिः applies equally to father and son; जाबालिः father, जाबालिः son; औद्वन्दरिः father, औद्वन्दरिः son; मापहीजङ्घेः father, मापहीजङ्घेः son. Here, first इङ् is added by IV. 1. 173, then फक् to denote Yuvan descendent. Then this फक् is elided by the present Vartika.

पैलादिभ्यश्च ॥ ५९ ॥ पदानि ॥ पैल-दादिभ्यः, च (युनि, लुग-शिजोः) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ पैल इरयेवमादिभ्यश्च युवमरयवस्य लुग् भवति ॥

59 And after the words पैल &c. there is the लुग् elision of the युवम् affix.

पीला + अच = पैलः (IV. 1. 118). 'The Gotra descendent of Paila.' पैलः + फिज् (IV. 1. 156). The present rule intervenes, and the Yuvan affix फिज् is elided; so पैल is both a Gotra and a Yuvan word. Some say that the 'Paila &c. words are formed by the affix इज्; (IV. 1. 95) and then the luk-elision of the Yuvan affix would be valid by the next rule 60. They would limit the scope of the present sūtra to cases where the Gotra of the people is not known, the Prachyas not being indicated.

इजः प्राचाम् ॥ ६० ॥ पदानि ॥ इजः, प्राचाम्, (युनि, लुग्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गोते च इज् तदन्ताद्वन्द्वस्यस्य लुग् भवति ॥

60. After a word ending with the Gotra affix इज् (IV. 1. 95) there is luk-elision of the Yuvan affix, when the Gotra of the people called Prachya (Eastern) is denoted.

पान्नागर + इज् = पान्नागरिः 'the Gotra descendent of Pannāgara'; after this the Yuvan affix फक् (IV. 1. 101) is elided by the present rule, and so पान्नागरिः is both the father and the son. So मान्मरैयचिः father and son. The word प्राचाम् here qualifies the word Gotra understood and does not show that it is an optional rule in the opinion of Eastern Grammarians. When the Gotra of Prachyas is not denoted, there is no elision. Thus दाचिः and दायायचः 'son of Dākshi.'

वृत्तिः ॥ तौलवलिभ्यः परस्य युग्मस्यस्य न लुग् भवति ॥

61. After the words तौलवलि and the rest there is not luk-elision of the Yuvan affix.

तौलवलिः is the name of the father and तौलवलायनः is the son of the former, formed by the Yuvan affix फक् (IV. 1. 101).

62. There is luk-elision of the तद्वाज (IV. 1. 174) affix, when the word is used in the plural number, provided that the plural number is taken by the base itself, and not by its standing as a compound epithet dependent upon another word, and provided that the base is not used in the feminine.

आङ्गः = अंग + अङ्ग (IV. 1. 170) 'a prince of Aṅga'; plural अङ्गः the princes of Aṅga. The affix अङ्ग is elided by present rule, and the Vriddhi vanishes with it too (I. 1. 63); but आङ्ग्यः 'the princesses of Aṅga,' plural of आङ्गि 'a princess of Aṅga.' But मिथवांगः 'he to whom the prince of Vanga is beloved' forms its plural मिथवांगः 'they whose beloved is the prince of Vanga,' there being no elision.

यस्कादिभ्यो गोत्रे ॥ ६३ ॥ पदानि ॥ यस्क-आदिभ्यः, गोत्रेः (बहुषुः तेनैवाख्तियाम् : लुग्) ॥

64. And there is luk-elision of the Gotra affixes यज् (IV. I. 105) and अज् (IV. I. 104) when the word is itself and not as part of a compound epithet dependent on another, takes the plural but not in the feminine.

गर्ग + यज् = गार्ग्यः; plural गर्गः 'the male descendents of Garga'. So also यस्काः 'the male descendents of Vatsa'; the singular being, यस्काः Similarly, विद + अज् = वैदः (IV. I. 104); plural विदाः and not वैदाः; similarly जीर्य singularly; जीर्याः plural.

But these affixes are not elided when the word forms part of a compound. Thus, मिग्गार्ग्यः 'those to whom Gārgya is beloved;' मिग्गैदः 'those to whom Baida is beloved.'

These affixes will not be elided in the feminine. Thus, गार्ग्यः, वैदः, feminine plurals.

Of course these affixes must be Gotra or patronymic affixes, otherwise there will be no elision. Thus द्वीप + यज् = द्वैप्यः 'living on the island,' plural द्वैप्यः; here the affix यज् is not elided as it does not denote a Gotra. So लस + अज् = जीरसः 'the pupil of Utsa,' plural जीरसः.

Virt:—In forming Tat-purusha compound of the singular and dual genitive, the affix यज् and अज् are optionally elided. Thus गार्ग्यस्य कुलं = गार्ग्यकुलं or गार्ग्यकुलं, गार्ग्ययोः कुलं = गार्ग्यकुलं or गार्ग्यकुलं.

338

ELISION OF GOTRA AFFIXES.

[Bk. II. Ch. IV. § 65, 66.

Similarly बैदस्वर व बैदयोः कुलं = बैदकुलं व बिदकुलं.

Why do we say 'the affixes यज् or अज्'? Because other affixes will not be elided in forming तत्पुरुष compound; such as आकृतुलं।

Why do we say 'singular or dual,'? Because in the plural तत्पुरुष compounds, these affixes must necessarily be elided and not optionally; thus गगनिकं कुलं = गगनकुलं.

Why do we say 'in forming तत्पुरुष compound'? Because in forming other compounds, these affixes will not be elided. Thus, उपगगनिकं which is an अव्ययीभाव compound, meaning गगनिकं समीपं. Of course, it is only in the Genitive तत्पुरुष that this rule is applicable; it will not therefore apply in कर्मचार्य तत्पुरुष &c., as परमागगनिकं।

अत्रिमृगुकुत्सवसिष्ठगोतनाङ्गिरीम्यश्च ॥ ६५ ॥ पदानि ॥ अत्रि-
मृगु-कुत्स-वसिष्ठ-गोतन-अङ्गिरीम्यः, च, (लुग्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ अव्ययादिभ्यः परस्य गोत्रप्रत्ययस्य बहुषु लुग् भवति ॥

65. And after the words अत्रि, मृगु, कुत्स, वसिष्ठ गोतम
अङ्गिरस there is luk-elision of the Gotra-affix, when the word takes the plural, but not in feminine.

Thus the plural of आत्रेय (अत्रि + इक् IV. 1. 122.) the descendent of अत्रि, is अत्रयः, the regular plural of अत्रि. So also, singular गगनिकं, plural मृगः; singular कौटः, plural कुत्साः; so, वसिष्ठाः, गोतमाः, अङ्गिरसः. In all these the affix has been elided. Thus मृगु + अज् = गगनिकं 'the descendent of Bhrigu. Of course, it is only in the plural number that the Gotra affixes इक् and अज् are elided, not in any other number; so we have in singular आत्रेयः गगनिकं; dual आत्रेयो गगनिकं; plural आत्रयः मृगः &c.

But when these words are part of a compound, the Gotra affixes are not elided in forming their plural. Thus प्रियात्रेयः or प्रियगगनिकः।

In the Feminine plural the affixes are not elided. Thus:—आत्रेयः प्रियः।

बहुवच इज प्राच्यभरतेषु ॥ ६६ ॥ पदानि ॥ बहुवचः, इजः प्राच्य-
भरतेषु, (बहुषु लुग्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ बहुवचः प्रतिपदिकाद् च इज विदितः प्राच्यगोत्रे भरतगोत्रे च वर्तते तस्य बहुषु
लुग् भवति ॥

66. There is luk-elision of the Gotra-affix इज् (IV., I. 95) after a word containing many vowels (a polysyllabic word) which denotes the Gotra of the people called प्राच्य and भरत when the word takes the plural.

BK. II. CH. IV. § 67, 68.]

ELISION OF GOTRA AFFIXES.

339

The plural of पन्नागारिः is पन्नागारः, there being elision of ब्रह्मः so also संवरेवलाः plural of गान्धरेवलिः; so the plural of यौपिष्टिरिः is युचिष्टिरः the descendents of Yudhishthira. But वैकिः and पौधिः not being polysyllabic, their plural will be वैकः and पौधः.

Why do we say 'when denoting the Gotra of Prāchyas and Bhāratas'? Because when denoting the Gotra of any other people, these affixes will not be elided. Thus बालाकः plural of बालाकिः, इल्लिदासः plural of इल्लिदासः.

Though the Bhāratas are Prāchyas, its specification here is to indicate that, wherever 'Prāchyas' will be used, it will not include Bhāratas as in V. 4 60. Here the Yuvan affix of Bhāratas will not be elided. Thus आर्जुनिः father, आर्जुनायनः son.

न गोपवनादिभ्यः ॥ ६७ ॥ पदानि ॥ न, गोप-वन-आदिभ्यः (लुग्), ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ गोपवनादिभ्यः परस्य प्रत्ययस्य लुग् न भवति ॥

67. After the words गोपवन, &c., there is not luk-elision of the Gotra affix, when the word takes the plural.

This prevents the application of II. 4. 64. Thus गोपवन + अण् = गोपवनः; plural गोपवनाः; singular वैकः, plural वैकः. The गोपवन &c., belong to Vidādi class, *vide* IV. 1. 104, and are the following:—गोपवन, चित्र, बिन्दु, भवन्, अस्य, अवतार, स्थानक and स्थापनः. The remaining words such as हरित &c., should not be taken in this sub-class. In the case of हरित &c., the Gotra affix must be elided in the plural by Rule 64. Thus हरिताः किंवदासः &c.

तिककितवादिभ्यो हन्तः ॥ ६८ ॥ पदानि ॥ तिक-कितव-

आदिभ्यः, हन्तः, (वहुल्लुग्) ॥

वृत्तिः ॥ तिकादिभ्यः कितवादिभ्यः हन्तः गोप-नत्ययस्य बहुव्र लुग् भवति ॥

68. After the words तिक कितव &c. when used as Dvandva compound, there is the luk-elision of the Gotra affixes, when the compound word takes the plural.

Thus तिक + फिज् = तैकायनिः (IV. 1. 154). Its plural is तैकायनयः तैकायनयः + कैतवायनयः = तिककितवाः। There is elision of फिज्. So also बालारिः plural बालारयः (IV. 1. 95) + बालारिरयः = बालारिरयः; there is elision of ब्रह्म (IV. 1. 95). The following is a list of such compounds.

1. तिककितवाः 2. बहुव्रलभण्डीरवाः 3. उपकलकाः (यौपकायनाः + लालकायनाः. IV. 1. 99, elision of कम्) 4. पक्कलकाः (पाककयः + नाककयः.

IV. 1. 95, elision of इज्). वकतलयुदपरिशद्भाः, 6. उष्मककुभाः (औष्मयः IV. 1. 95. + काकुभाः IV. 1. 112, then the elision of इज् and अण्). 7. सङ्ग्रान्त-युष्माः (the elision of इज् IV. 9. 95 as in 4). 8. उष्मसंकटाः (औरसायनयः IV. 1. 154 + सांकटयः IV. 1. 95, elision of फिज् and इज्). 9. प्रहक कपिह्लाः (elision of इज् as in 4). 10. कृष्णाजिनकृष्णयुद्राः (elision of इज्). 11. अन्वेष—दासेरकाः (आधिवेषयः IV. 1. 105 + दासेरकयः IV. 1. 95, elision of both यज् and इज्).
